DONE (2026-10-10) "Realtime": I chose "trigger a cursor pull per household", so pull stays the only path that applies remote rows. Server: new migration `20261010150000_realtime.sql` adds the 8 household tables, `household_members`, `categories`, the 3 per-user tables and `ingredients` to the `supabase_realtime` publication. Realtime then applies each subscriber's RLS select policies. Replica identity stays the default (primary key). Client: new `src/sync/realtime.ts`, `startRealtime(userId)`, started from `AppDataGate` while signed in. It opens one channel per household (each household table filtered `household_id=eq.<id>`, or `id=eq.` for `households`), a user channel (`household_members` and the user's 4 own tables, filtered to the user) and a catalog channel (`ingredients`). An event schedules a scoped pull. Events within `REALTIME_BATCH_MS` (300 ms) of the first share one pull. A household event pulls that household, a user-table event pulls the user's tables, and a catalog event pulls the catalog. A `household_members` event for this user does a full pull. Each full pull reports the memberships it read through the new `onMemberships`, and channels are opened and closed to match. Each channel pulls its scope once SUBSCRIBED, which covers the gap since the last pull and rejoins after errors. Background or offline closes every channel. Foreground reopens them, and a reconnect replaces them with new ones. An event that arrives on a channel after it has closed is ignored. `pull.ts` changes: `pullNow({ scope })` with `PullScope` (`households`, `user`, `catalog`). A scoped run doesn't read memberships. Coalescing now merges the scopes asked for during a run (`mergeScopes`), and a full request makes the next run full. I also added `applyRemoteDelete`, which fills the gap the pull task left: Realtime DELETE events for the user's `user_category_order`/`user_category_overrides` rows (hard-deleted, so pull can't see them) delete the local row from the event's key, unless the outbox has an unpushed change for it. Delete events can't be filtered, so other users' deletes arrive and are ignored, including other members' `household_members` deletes. The remote check animates like a local one with no UI change: the list's `useLiveQueryOn` re-runs on any SQLite change, and the row's Reanimated layout/entering animations don't care where the write came from. Known gaps for the Membership task: a lost membership only closes that household's channel. Its local rows and outbox entries stay until that task's purge. Household hard-deletes (cascades) just trigger a pull of that household. Spec 7.2 has a "Realtime" client note. Tests added: `src/sync/__tests__/realtime.test.ts` (20), which drives the real pull against a fake server: which channels open and their exact bindings/filters; channels before and after memberships are known; not configured opens none; cleanup closes all and cancels a scheduled pull; a remote check comes down within the batch window through the pull (only that household's 8 tables queried, local item checked); several events share one pull and two households pull both; another household's change isn't delivered; user-table and catalog events pull only those; a deleted override is applied without a pull while another user's delete is ignored; SUBSCRIBED catches up per channel; CHANNEL_ERROR just warns; joining a household does a full pull and opens its channel; losing one closes only that channel; another member's removal is ignored; background/foreground, starting in the background, offline/reconnect (new channels) and staying online (same channels); events on closed channels do nothing. In `pull.test.ts` (13 new): `mergeScopes`; household-, user- and catalog-scoped pulls query exactly those tables; an empty scope; scoped calls during a run merged into one more run; a full request upgrades the next run; `onMemberships` (each full pull, replay for the same user only, scoped pulls silent, unsubscribe, a failed lookup reports nothing); `applyRemoteDelete` (deletes without an outbox write, keeps a row with an unpushed change, ignores another user/missing row/incomplete key/other tables, order rows). Also new: `supabase/tests/09_realtime.test.sql` (exactly these tables published, no private tables, default replica identity). goal: Goal: a small web app, run locally against hosted Supabase, for the jobs the dashboard makes awkward: find a user and change their plan, edit what each plan includes and its monthly limits, and see how much of each AI feature people use. It lives in `admin/` in this repo. The dashboard and the `admin.*` SQL snippets stay for everything else (deleting a user, reading logs). ### Decisions - **Who is an admin**: a `private.admins (user_id)` table and `public.is_admin()`, not a role in the JWT, so removing an admin takes effect at once. Admins are added and removed in the Table Editor. - **The server checks every action.** The portal holds only the project URL and publishable key and signs in like the app does. Every admin action is a `public.admin_*` SQL function (`security definer`) whose first step is `private.require_admin()`, which raises `not authorized` (`42501`) for anyone else; execute is granted to `authenticated` only. The `admin` schema and its revokes don't change: the dashboard snippets keep working, and portal functions write `admin.admin_actions` with `performed_by` set explicitly to `auth.uid()::text` (the column defaults to `session_user`, which is `authenticator` for an API call). Rows from the dashboard keep `postgres`; the portal shows them as "Dashboard". The login screen is only UX. - **Sign-in is Google**, the same provider as the app, through Supabase's OAuth redirect. Not email codes: turning on email sign-in on hosted would let anyone create an account by email. Against local Supabase the portal also offers the email code (the code arrives in the local mail viewer, as for the app's dev stub). - **Usage comes from the existing per-user usage tables**, which the Plans section keeps for 40 days and counts on every plan. So the portal shows this month and a 40-day daily series; there's no longer history. Counts only: no prompts, links or names. `ai_calls` still has no user id (6.5). - **Plans are edited as data.** The six feature keys are fixed in code (each is enforced by an Edge Function); the portal combines them into plans and sets their limits. A plan that has `recipe_import` or `recipe_import_photo` must have `categorize`, enforced by a trigger so Table Editor edits obey it too. - **`admin/` is its own Yarn project** (own `package.json` and `yarn.lock`), not a workspace, so Next.js's React can't clash with Expo's in a hoisted `node_modules`. The root's TypeScript, ESLint, Jest and Metro ignore it. ### Look: "Pantry, back office" Recognisably the app, made for a laptop. Same as the app: Bricolage Grotesque titles (800, −0.025 em) over Figtree, soft white cards on the pale green ground, round initial avatars, light and dark following the system, and DESIGN.md's colours as CSS variables (no hex in components). Different: a deep-green sidebar (the app's `primary`, darkened) with white text and a small "Back office" pill beside "The Perfect Bite"; dense tables with hairline rows and tabular figures; and each AI feature keeps one aisle colour everywhere (usage tiles, charts, plan grid), so it reads at a glance. No floating tab bar, no phone frames. ### Database ### Portal

goal: Goal: a small web app, run locally against hosted Supabase, for the jobs the dashboard makes awkward: find a user and change their plan, edit what each plan includes and its monthly limits, and see how much of each AI feature people use. It lives in `admin/` in this repo. The dashboard and the `admin.*` SQL snippets stay for everything else (deleting a user, reading logs). ### Decisions - **Who is an admin**: a `private.admins (user_id)` table and `public.is_admin()`, not a role in the JWT, so removing an admin takes effect at once. Admins are added and removed in the Table Editor. - **The server checks every action.** The portal holds only the project URL and publishable key and signs in like the app does. Every admin action is a `public.admin_*` SQL function (`security definer`) whose first step is `private.require_admin()`, which raises `not authorized` (`42501`) for anyone else; execute is granted to `authenticated` only. The `admin` schema and its revokes don't change: the dashboard snippets keep working, and portal functions write `admin.admin_actions` with `performed_by` set explicitly to `auth.uid()::text` (the column defaults to `session_user`, which is `authenticator` for an API call). Rows from the dashboard keep `postgres`; the portal shows them as "Dashboard". The login screen is only UX. - **Sign-in is Google**, the same provider as the app, through Supabase's OAuth redirect. Not email codes: turning on email sign-in on hosted would let anyone create an account by email. Against local Supabase the portal also offers the email code (the code arrives in the local mail viewer, as for the app's dev stub). - **Usage comes from the existing per-user usage tables**, which the Plans section keeps for 40 days and counts on every plan. So the portal shows this month and a 40-day daily series; there's no longer history. Counts only: no prompts, links or names. `ai_calls` still has no user id (6.5). - **Plans are edited as data.** The six feature keys are fixed in code (each is enforced by an Edge Function); the portal combines them into plans and sets their limits. A plan that has `recipe_import` or `recipe_import_photo` must have `categorize`, enforced by a trigger so Table Editor edits obey it too. - **`admin/` is its own Yarn project** (own `package.json` and `yarn.lock`), not a workspace, so Next.js's React can't clash with Expo's in a hoisted `node_modules`. The root's TypeScript, ESLint, Jest and Metro ignore it. ### Look: "Pantry, back office" Recognisably the app, made for a laptop. Same as the app: Bricolage Grotesque titles (800, −0.025 em) over Figtree, soft white cards on the pale green ground, round initial avatars, light and dark following the system, and DESIGN.md's colours as CSS variables (no hex in components). Different: a deep-green sidebar (the app's `primary`, darkened) with white text and a small "Back office" pill beside "The Perfect Bite"; dense tables with hairline rows and tabular figures; and each AI feature keeps one aisle colour everywhere (usage tiles, charts, plan grid), so it reads at a glance. No floating tab bar, no phone frames. ### Database ### Portal

Precedence: signed out "Not syncing" > offline "Offline" > push/pull running "Syncing…" > a standing push/pull error "Sync error" (push first, shown as "Sending: …" / "Receiving: …") > pending outbox "Syncing…" > never synced "Not synced yet" > "Synced". The file also has `formatLastSync`, `outboxCounts` (pending vs rejected), `readSyncInputs` and `syncNow` (a forced push, then a full pull). The filter is `components/action-filter.tsx`, a client `<select>` that does `router.replace` to `?action=` and goes back to page 1; an unknown `?action=` is kept as an extra option. The wording is in `admin/lib/activity.ts`. Labels: Changed plan, Changed a limit, Changed a feature, Created a plan, Renamed a plan, Changed the default plan, Deleted a plan, Deleted user, Deleted own account, and the raw name for anything else. Target: the user's email linking to `/users/[id]`, else the plan id, else the household id; then (my addition) a deleted user's raw id, unlinked; else "—". Summaries: set_user_plan "plus → unlimited" (null as "default"); set_plan_limit and set_plan_feature from the before/after snapshots ("recipe_import limit 40 → 60", "recipe_tags added, limit no limit", "recipe_import removed", "No change"; raw feature keys, as in the task's example); create_plan "“Pro” · 2 features"; rename_plan "“Plus” → “Plus+”"; set_default_plan "base → plus" ("none" when there was no default); delete_plan "“Old” · 0 users"; delete_user "<email> · 3 households: 1 promoted, 2 deleted"; delete_account "1 household: 1 left"; an unknown action shows its details as compact JSON cut to 80 characters. Who: the admin's email, "Dashboard" for `postgres`, otherwise the raw value. One choice of mine: `delete_account` shows "The user", because the app's row has `performed_by` set to the session user (e.g. `authenticator`). Paging reuses `parsePage`, `parseQuery` and `pageRange` from `lib/users.ts`. Vitest `admin/lib/activity.test.ts` (22 tests) covers: every label and an unknown one (including `toString`); filter options; URLs; each action's summary with edge cases (null default, no limit, thousands, no change, added/removed, singulars, no households, malformed details) and the unknown one (JSON, truncation, empty); the target's order and fallbacks; who. Checks: portal test (139 passed), lint, tsc, build; root jest (5203 passed), lint, tsc. Not run against a dev server or local Supabase. No real AI calls. NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK (in manual-checks.md).
manualChecks: The portal's look and shell: run `yarn admin` and open http://localhost:3000 (it goes to /users) in a browser with the system in light, then dark. Check: the deep-green sidebar with the gold cloche, "The Perfect Bite" in Bricolage Grotesque and the "Back office" pill on one line; Users, Plans, AI usage and Activity each open their empty page, titled in Bricolage 800 on the pale green ground, with the current one highlighted in the sidebar; body text is Figtree.

goal: Goal: see why AI calls fail, and find people misusing the AI, e.g. a fake recipe written to get an explicit AI photo, with who did it and exactly what we sent the model. `public.ai_calls` already has one row per model attempt by `runAiTask`, with its `status`, `error`, instructions and prompt, but no user id (by design until now), a provider error keeps only the SDK's message, the AI photo's image call (`generateImage`, OpenAI Images) isn't recorded at all, and the portal shows only counts. A photo description that answers `isFood: false` is an `ok` call, so it has to be flagged on purpose, not found among the failures. The spec changes with this: `ai_calls` now records who made each call, and admins can read any call's instructions, prompt and response in the portal (each read is audited) and see the AI photos that were made, since a harmful photo the image model allowed is never flagged. Rows still expire after 30 days, except flagged calls and the calls linked to them, kept 180 days. Emailing the owner about flags (Resend) comes later; not in these tasks.
title: `ai_calls` records who made each call
text: `ai_calls` records who made each call (spec 5, 6.4, 6.5). Migration: add `user_id uuid references auth.users on delete set null` and `household_id uuid references public.households on delete set null` to `public.ai_calls`, with an index on `(user_id, created_at desc)`. Add both to `AiCallRecord` (`supabase/functions/_shared/ai/run-ai-task.ts`) and a `RunAiTaskOptions.caller?: { userId: string; householdId: string | null }` that `runAiTask` copies onto every attempt's record (null without it). Every function that calls a model passes the signed-in caller it already resolves for its feature and limit checks, and the household when the request has one: `categorize-ingredients` (including categorizing inside `import-recipe` and `import-recipe-photo`), `import-recipe`, `import-recipe-photo`, `match-recipe-steps`, `suggest-recipe-tags`, `generate-recipe-photo` (`describeRecipePhoto`). The `yarn ai:*` scripts and evals pass nothing, so their rows have nulls. Deno tests: each handler's test checks its logged rows carry the user (and household where there is one); `runAiTask` with no `caller` records nulls. pgTAP: deleting a user nulls `user_id` and keeps the row. Update spec 5 and 6.4 (the `ai_calls` lines) and 6.5 and every "`ai_calls` stores … but no user id" Privacy line (6.6–6.11): rows now have the user and household, are still service role only, and still expire after 30 days. In `docs/alpha-testing.md`, the privacy policy line also says the policy must disclose that what's sent to the AI is logged with the account and kept 30 days (180 for flagged calls), and that admins can read it.
notes: `ai_calls` records who made each call (2026-10-19, spec 5, 6.4, 6.5): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261119120000_ai_calls_caller.sql` adds `user_id` (→ `auth.users`, on delete set null) and `household_id` (→ `households`, on delete set null) with an index on `(user_id, created_at desc)`. `run-ai-task.ts` exports `AiCaller = { userId, householdId | null }`; `AiCallRecord` gains `user_id`/`household_id`, and `RunAiTaskOptions.caller?` is copied onto every attempt (primary and fallback, ok or failed), nulls without it. Wiring: `categorize(names, store, model?, caller?)` (a 4th positional parameter, so the 45 existing `categorize(…, store, model)` calls didn't change); `caller?` on `ImportDeps`, `PhotoImportDeps`, `SuggestDeps`, `MatchDeps`/`MatchStepsDeps` and `DescribeOptions`; `GenerateDeps.userId?`, with the household taken from the reservation. Each `index.ts` passes `{ userId, householdId: null }` (only AI photos have a household), and import-recipe / import-recipe-photo pass it to the inline categorize too. CLIs and evals pass nothing, so their rows have nulls. Updated the "no user id" comments in the stores, spec 5 (server-only tables), 6.4's Privacy bullet, 6.5 (a new paragraph on `ai_calls`), the Privacy lines of 6.6, 6.7, 6.8, 6.10 and 6.11, `docs/admin.md`, and the privacy policy line in `docs/alpha-testing.md` (logged with the account, 30 days, 180 for flagged calls, admins can read it). Existing tests changed because the behavior changed: `06_ai_calls.test.sql` checked `hasnt_column user_id`; it now checks the columns, nullability, the index and the FK, that deleting the user nulls `user_id` and keeps the row and its household, and that deleting the household nulls `household_id` and keeps the user (plan 9 → 20). The suggest-recipe-tags and match-recipe-steps "no user id" tests asserted `!('user_id' in call)`; they now assert the caller's user id and a null household. `categorize-ingredients/cli.test.ts`'s record fixture got the two fields. New Deno tests: `ai.test.ts` (the caller on both the failed primary and the fallback; a caller with no household; no caller gives nulls on ok and on failure), categorize `handler.test.ts` (caller on ok and invalid_output rows; nulls without one), import-recipe and import-recipe-photo (the extraction and inline categorize rows carry the user with a null household; photo import also a failed extraction), suggest-recipe-tags and match-recipe-steps (a failed call carries the caller too), generate-recipe-photo (the description row has the user and the recipe's household, a failed description too, nulls with no caller). Checks: Deno tests in categorize-ingredients (295), import-recipe (177), import-recipe-photo (64), match-recipe-steps (61), suggest-recipe-tags (59), generate-recipe-photo (51), all pass; every edited `index.ts`, CLI and eval type-checks; `supabase db reset` and `supabase test db` (1623 passed); root jest (5205 passed), lint, tsc. No real AI calls.

title: Failed AI calls keep the provider's answer
text: Failed AI calls keep the provider's answer (spec 5, 6.4). Migration: add `http_status integer` and `error_body text` to `public.ai_calls` (null on `ok` rows and on failures with no HTTP answer). In `run-ai-task.ts`, add both to `AiCallRecord`; a failed attempt sets `http_status` from `apiCallError(err)?.statusCode` and `error_body` from its `responseBody` (cut to 4000 characters), and `error` keeps its current `name: message` text (2000). Deno tests: a mock model that throws an `APICallError` (status 529, a JSON body) records both; one wrapped in a `RetryError` records the last error's; invalid output and a timeout record nulls; an `ok` attempt records nulls. Safety blocks: find out from the AI SDK provider source (`@ai-sdk/google`, `@ai-sdk/openai` as the functions import them) how a blocked call comes back for the providers we use: Gemini's blocked prompt (`promptFeedback.blockReason`) or `SAFETY` finish, and an OpenAI structured-output `refusal`. Every such attempt, whatever its status, records `finish_reason` `content-filter` (map it in `runAiTask` if the SDK reports it another way or loses it on a thrown error), so the flag in the task below catches it. Deno tests: a mock model reproducing each shape records `content-filter`. Say in spec 6.4 how a safety block is recorded.
notes: Failed AI calls keep the provider's answer (2026-10-19, spec 5, 6.4): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261120120000_ai_calls_error_body.sql` adds `http_status integer` and `error_body text` to `ai_calls`. `AiCallRecord` gains both; a failed attempt takes them from `apiCallError(err)` (an `APICallError`, or a `RetryError`'s last one): `statusCode` and `responseBody` cut to 4000; `error` is unchanged (`name: message`, 2000); ok rows and failures with no HTTP answer have nulls. Safety blocks: the provider source wasn't readable from the sandbox (the Deno npm cache is outside the repo), so I ran the real `@ai-sdk/google@4.0.88`, `@ai-sdk/anthropic@4.0.72` and `@ai-sdk/openai@4.0.96` against a fake `fetch` returning blocked bodies in a throwaway Deno test. Gemini's `promptFeedback.blockReason` (SAFETY, PROHIBITED_CONTENT) and `SAFETY`/`PROHIBITED_CONTENT` candidate finishes, and Anthropic's `stop_reason: 'refusal'`, all come back as finish reason `content-filter` (raw = the provider's reason) with no output, which `runAiTask` already turns into an `invalid_output` row that keeps the finish reason, so no mapping was needed (a comment says so). The task names `@ai-sdk/openai`, but no function imports it: the language-model providers are Google and Anthropic, and OpenAI is only the image call's plain `fetch` (next task). For the record, `@ai-sdk/openai` reports a chat `refusal` as finish `stop` with empty text and drops the refusal; I didn't map that, since mapping "empty + stop" to `content-filter` would wrongly flag other empty answers and the shape can't reach `runAiTask`. Spec 5 (`ai_calls` line) and 6.4 (new "What a failed attempt records" and "Safety blocks" bullets) say all this. Tests: Deno `categorize-ingredients/ai.test.ts` gets an APICallError 529 with a JSON body records both columns and the error text; a long body/error is cut to 4000/2000; no body gives a status and a null body; a RetryError (503 then 529) records the last error's; invalid output, a timeout (`TimeoutError`) and an ok attempt record nulls; five mock shapes reproducing the probed safety blocks (Gemini blocked prompt, prohibited prompt, SAFETY finish, SAFETY after partial JSON, Anthropic refusal) each record `invalid_output` + `content-filter`; a safety block doesn't try the fallback. `cli.test.ts`'s record helper gets the two new fields (type change only). pgTAP `06_ai_calls`: both columns' types, nulls when unset, and a failed row stores 529 and its body (plan 20 → 25). Deno suites: categorize-ingredients (308), import-recipe (177), import-recipe-photo (64), match-recipe-steps (61), suggest-recipe-tags (59), generate-recipe-photo (51), all pass; `supabase db reset` + `supabase test db` pass; root jest (5205 passed), lint, tsc pass. No real AI calls (the probe used a fake fetch). Cleanup needed: the sandbox wouldn't let me delete the scratch files `.probe/probe.ts` and `supabase/functions/categorize-ingredients/zz-probe.test.ts` (emptied); delete both, they aren't part of the change.

title: The AI photo's image call goes into `ai_calls`
text: The AI photo's image call goes into `ai_calls` (spec 6.11, 6.4). Add `refused` to the `ai_calls.status` check, to `private.ai_call_stats`'s `statuses` (zeros included) and to the portal's `AiCallStatus` / `STATUS_ORDER` (`admin/lib/types.ts`, `admin/lib/ai-usage.ts`). In `supabase/functions/generate-recipe-photo/image.ts`, `ImageFailedError` and `ImageRefusedError` carry the HTTP status and the response body when there was one. `handler.ts` logs one row per image call through `store.logAiCall`, success or failure, with the caller as above: `task` `recipePhotoImage`, `model` named the way the other rows name theirs, `prompt_version` `RECIPE_PHOTO_IMAGE_PROMPT_VERSION`, `instructions` empty, `prompt` the image prompt, `output` `{ quality, path }` on success (the photo's Storage path in `recipe-photos`; never the image bytes), the token counts from `usage`, `duration_ms`, `fallback_of` the description row's id (so the two steps link), and on failure `error`, `http_status` and `error_body` (4000). Status: a content-policy refusal `refused`; an HTTP error `api_error`; the timeout `timeout`; no image or bad base64 `invalid_output`; anything else (no key, `off`) `error`. Both AI photo rows (description and image) also record the recipe: migration adds `recipe_id uuid references public.recipes on delete set null` to `public.ai_calls`, `AiCallRecord` gains it and `RunAiTaskOptions.recipeId?` is copied onto each attempt like `caller` (null for every other task). The mock model logs too. A failure to log never fails the request (log it, like `ai_call_log_failed`). pgTAP: `refused` is accepted and counted by `ai_call_stats`. Deno tests (`generate-recipe-photo/handler.test.ts`): a generated photo logs the description row and an `ok` image row linked to it, both with the recipe id, the image row with the photo's path; a refusal, a 500 and a timeout each log the right status with the HTTP status and body; the image bytes are never in a row. Update spec 6.4 ("one row per model attempt") and 6.11's Privacy line. (If `fallback_of` reads wrong for the link, add a `parent_id` column instead and say so in the spec.)
notes: The AI photo's image call goes into `ai_calls` (2026-10-19, spec 6.4, 6.11): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261121120000_ai_calls_image.sql`: `refused` added to the `ai_calls.status` check; `recipe_id uuid references public.recipes on delete set null`; `private.ai_call_stats` counts `refused` (zeros included) and leaves `recipePhotoImage` rows out of `fallbacks`, since their `fallback_of` is the link to the description, not a fallback. I kept `fallback_of` for the link (no `parent_id`), as the next tasks' retention and `primary`/`fallback` build on it; the spec says so. `run-ai-task.ts`: `AiCallRecord` gains `recipe_id`, `task` may be `RECIPE_PHOTO_IMAGE_TASK` (`recipePhotoImage`), status may be `refused`; `RunAiTaskOptions.recipeId?` is copied onto each attempt (null otherwise). `image.ts`: `ImageRefusedError` and `ImageFailedError` carry `httpStatus` and `body` (the raw text of a failed answer; a 200's body is never kept, since it holds the image), and `ImageFailedError.failure` is the row's status (HTTP or network error `api_error`, timeout `timeout`, no image/bad base64 `invalid_output`, no key/`off` `error`); new `imageModelId` (`openai:<model>`, `mock` stays `mock`). `describe.ts` takes `recipeId` and returns the answering row's `callId`. `handler.ts` writes one `recipePhotoImage` row per image call (success, refusal, failure) with the caller, household, recipe, empty instructions, the image prompt, `{ quality, path }` on success (the row is written before the upload), tokens, duration, `fallback_of` the description row, and `error`/`http_status`/`error_body` (4000) on failure. A failed write logs `ai_call_log_failed` and never fails the request. Portal: `AiCallStatus`/`STATUS_ORDER` gain `refused` (between timeout and error). Spec: 5 (`ai_calls` line: image rows, statuses, `recipe_id`), 4.12 (AI usage counts), 6.4 (new "One row per model attempt, and per image call" bullet), 6.11 Privacy. New tests: Deno `handler.test.ts` (the ok image row checked in full and linked to the description, both rows with the recipe id; an upper-case recipe id is lowercased; the mock image model logs `mock` with no tokens; a refusal, a 500 and a timeout through the real `generateImage` over a fake fetch log `refused`/400, `api_error`/500 and `timeout`/nulls with their errors and bodies; a 5000-char body is cut to 4000; `invalid_output` and no-key `error`; the image bytes and base64 are never in a row; a throwing `logAiCall` doesn't fail a success or a refusal; isFood false and a failed description log no image row), `image.test.ts` (what each error carries, including a non-JSON and an empty body; `imageModelId`). Existing tests I changed because the behavior changed: four handler tests now expect the second `ai_call` step/row; admin `ai-usage.test.ts`'s "status this portal doesn't know" uses `blocked` now that `refused` is known (plus a new ordering test), and its fixtures have `refused: 0`; pgTAP `51_admin_ai_usage` expects `"refused": 0`; `categorize-ingredients/cli.test.ts`'s record helper gets `recipe_id` (type only). pgTAP `06_ai_calls` (25 → 31 tests): `recipe_id` type and nullable, `refused` accepted, `ai_call_stats` counts it with no image fallback, the FK, deleting the recipe nulls `recipe_id`. Checks: Deno generate-recipe-photo (65), categorize-ingredients (308), import-recipe (177), import-recipe-photo (64), match-recipe-steps (61), suggest-recipe-tags (59) pass; every touched `index.ts`, CLI and the photo eval type-check (`deno test --no-run`, since `deno check` needs approval here); `supabase db reset` + `supabase test db` (1634) pass; root jest (5205), lint, tsc pass; admin vitest (140), tsc, lint pass. No real AI calls. The scratch files `.probe/probe.ts` and `supabase/functions/categorize-ingredients/zz-probe.test.ts` from the last task are still there; delete them by hand.

title: Flagged AI calls
text: Flagged AI calls (spec 4.12, 6.11). One SQL function decides what's flagged, `private.ai_call_flag(public.ai_calls) returns text` (immutable): `not_food` for a `recipePhotoDescription` row whose `output->>'isFood'` is `'false'`, `refused` for a `refused` row, `content_filter` for a `content-filter` `finish_reason` (any task), else null. Use it in a partial index for the flagged rows. Spec 6.11: when the description says the recipe isn't food, the call is flagged (it still answers `not_food` and gives the slot back, as now). Add the rule to spec 4.12 beside the portal functions below. Retention: replace the `ai-calls-retention` job's command so a row is deleted after 30 days unless it, or a row whose `fallback_of` is its id, or the row its `fallback_of` points to, is flagged; those go after 180 days (so a refused image keeps the description holding the recipe the user wrote, and the other way round). Deleting the account still nulls `user_id`: no copy of who made it is kept. Update spec 5, 6.4 and 6.5 (and the Privacy lines changed above) to say flagged calls and their linked calls are kept 180 days. pgTAP: each flag case, an `isFood: true` description and an ordinary failure are not flagged; the job's command (run directly) deletes a 31-day-old unflagged row, keeps a 31-day-old flagged row and the row linked to it, and deletes both at 181 days.
notes: Flagged AI calls (2026-10-19, spec 4.12, 6.11): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261122120000_ai_calls_flags.sql`: `private.ai_call_flag(public.ai_calls)` (sql, immutable, revoked from public/anon/authenticated) answers `not_food` (a `recipePhotoDescription` row with `output->>'isFood' = 'false'`), `refused` (status `refused`), `content_filter` (finish reason `content-filter`, any task), else null, checked in that order; partial index `ai_calls_flagged_idx` on `(created_at desc) where private.ai_call_flag(ai_calls) is not null`; plus `ai_calls_fallback_of_idx` (partial, on `fallback_of`) for the retention lookups and the next task's `recovered`/`fallback`. `ai-calls-retention` is rescheduled under the same name (pg_cron replaces the command and keeps `17 3 * * *`): delete after 30 days unless the row, the row its `fallback_of` points to, or a row whose `fallback_of` is its id is flagged; those go after 180 days. User deletion still just nulls `user_id` (unchanged). No app or function code changed: `generate-recipe-photo` already answers `not_food` and releases the slot. Spec: 4.12 new **Flagged AI calls** bullet after AI usage (the portal functions come in the next task); 5 (server-only tables line and the `ai_calls` retention sentence); 6.4 Privacy; 6.5; 6.6, 6.7, 6.8, 6.10 and 6.11 Privacy lines say 180 days when flagged or linked; 6.11 step 6 says the `not_food` row is flagged. New pgTAP `54_ai_call_flags` (20 tests): each flag case, `isFood: true`, an ordinary failure and `isFood: false` on another task not flagged, the function is immutable and not callable by `authenticated`, the partial index exists with its predicate; running the job's command from `cron.job` directly: one job with its schedule kept, a 31-day unflagged row deleted, a 29-day row kept, a 31-day refused image kept with its description, a 31-day `not_food` primary kept with the row linking to it, a flagged pair at 181 days both deleted, a 179-day flagged row kept. Checks: `supabase db reset` + `supabase test db` (1654) pass; root jest (5205), lint, tsc pass. No real AI calls. (`/tmp/pbspec/edit.py` is an unused scratch file outside the repo.)

text: Portal functions for failed and flagged AI calls (spec 4.12). Since it shows a user's own text, it writes one `admin.admin_actions` row per call (`action` `view_ai_call`, `target_user_id` the call's user, `details` `{ ai_call_id, task, flag }`, no note, `performed_by` the admin's id, as the plan functions set it), so it isn't `stable`. `admin_user_detail` gains `ai_flags`: the user's flagged calls in the last 30 days, a count per flag. Update spec 4.12 (a bullet after **AI usage**): admins can read any call's instructions, prompt and response, and who made it, and see the AI photos made, in the portal; opening a call is audited. Update the **Activity** bullet's list of what writes `admin_actions`, and spec 5's storage policies.

title: The index card recipe view
text: The index card recipe view (spec 4.5, board F `docs/design/recipe-view/f-index-card.png`). When `useRecipeViewStyle()` is `indexCard`, `src/app/recipe/[id]/index.tsx` renders `RecipeIndexCard` (`src/features/recipes/recipe-index-card.tsx`) in its scroll view in place of the photo header, band, switch and cards; the header's ⋯ menu, the `RecipeActionDock` (with Plan, its toasts and hidden-while-adding), the add bar, the toasts, servings state (`chosen`), the ingredient add/edit/delete/long-press handlers and the Method picks all stay in the screen and are passed in, so both views behave the same. On a plain `background` (no tinted band, header not transparent, `headerStyle` `background`, no shadow), 20 pt side margins: **Top row**: the name in `screenTitle` (`accessibilityRole` header), wrapping, beside a 64 × 64 pt square (`rounded.lg`, cover) at its top right with `spacing.lg` between: the photo (the household's own, else the site's, as now; uploading shows the device's copy) over the recipe's tile colour (`aisles[hue].soft`), which shows alone with no photo, while it loads and if it fails; tapping it opens the Choose a photo sheet (VoiceOver "Add photo" or "Change photo"); while Generate with AI runs, a small spinner in it. The plan badges (`PlanBadges`) under the name. **Source line**: the link's host without `www.` (`recipeLinkParts`) in `aisles[hue].strong` `headline`, opening Safari, then " · " in `inkSecondary`, then "for 4" (`forServingsLabel`, the stepper's servings) in `ink` `headline` with a 2 pt `aisles[hue].soft` underline; tapping "for 4" swaps it for the same `Stepper` (and **Reset** when off the recipe's servings) the Ingredients card has. No link: just the servings; no servings: a dashed **Add servings** pill as now; neither: no line. The link is edited from the standard view only. **Notes**: in `lead` italic, `aisles[hue].strong`, inside curly quotes, all of it (no line limit); tap to edit as the band's notes do; no notes: the "+ Add notes" row as now. Tags aren't shown. A hairline `separator` under that, `spacing.lg` above and below. **Ingredients**, no card, no aisle dots: one row per ingredient, at least `minTapTarget` tall, the amount (`formatAmount`, or scaled to the stepper's servings) right-aligned in `inkSecondary` `body` in a fixed column (the widest amount, measured, capped at 40% of the width) and the name (`displayItemName`, then the note in `inkSecondary`) in `ink` `body`, `spacing.md` between. A row keeps tap to edit, long-press to add to a list (and its VoiceOver action) and swipe left to delete, so factor `RecipeIngredientRow`'s gestures out or give it a `layout` prop rather than copying them. Then "+ Add ingredient" (`AddIngredientRow`). No ingredients: the same empty text as the card. **Method**: with steps, "Method, 8 steps" and a `chevron.right` in `aisles[hue].strong` `headline` (`stepPath`'s count, as the switch counts it); a tap shows the `RecipeMethodCard` under it, with the line turning to "Hide method" and a `chevron.down`, kept while the screen is open (VoiceOver: a button with the expanded state). No steps: the Method card as the standard view shows it with none (its Add steps). The content ends above the dock as now. Strings in `en.ts` and `es.ts`. Jest (`src/features/recipes/__tests__/`): the setting picks the view, and switching it on an open screen swaps the view; the source line with a link and servings, servings only, neither; tapping "for 4" shows the stepper and scales the amounts; the amount column right-aligns; the method line's count, expanding and its VoiceOver state; the photo square's photo, tile colour, and its tap opens the sheet; the dock still shows Add to a list, Cook and Plan. Update spec 4.5's **Recipe view trial** bullet with the layout. text: The plan modal adds instead of replacing (spec 4.16 Plan from a recipe). section: Safety identifier on the photo call
title: Send a hashed user id as `safety_identifier` on the OpenAI image call, so OpenAI can attribute a content-policy violation to the end user
text: Send a hashed user id as `safety_identifier` on the OpenAI image call, so OpenAI can attribute a content-policy violation to the end user (and block that identifier) rather than only to our org. `image.ts`: `ImageOptions` gains an optional `safetyIdentifier?: string`, and `generateImage` adds `safety_identifier` to the request body when it's set (left out when not, never `null` or `""`). `handler.ts` (line ~177): the default `generate` passes `safetyIdentifier` from `deps.userId`, hashed as the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the user id (`crypto.subtle.digest`, a small helper in `image.ts`); no user id, no identifier. The raw user id never goes to OpenAI. The mock and off models are unchanged, and the CLI sends none. Deno tests (`image.test.ts`, `handler.test.ts`): the body has the identifier when given and lacks the key when not; the handler sends the hash of `USER_ID` (64 hex chars, not the id itself); the identifier is the same for the same user across calls.
notes: Safety identifier on the photo call (2026-10-21, spec 6.11): DONE, checked off. `image.ts`: `ImageOptions.safetyIdentifier?`, sent as `safety_identifier` only when set and non-empty (never null or ""); new `safetyIdentifierFor(userId)`, the lowercase hex SHA-256 via `crypto.subtle.digest`. `handler.ts`: the `generateImage` dep now takes `(prompt, { safetyIdentifier? })`; the handler hashes `deps.userId` (no caller, no identifier) and the default forwards it to the real call, so the raw id never goes to OpenAI. Mock/off models and the CLI unchanged (the CLI's dep ignores the second argument). Deno tests: `image.test.ts` (identifier in the body; key absent for undefined and ""; the hash matches the SHA-256 "abc" vector, is 64 hex, stable, differs per id); `handler.test.ts` (the body sent to a fake OpenAI carries `safetyIdentifierFor(USER_ID)`, 64 hex, not the id, and the id appears nowhere in the body; same identifier across two calls; no caller → no key). Test helpers changed, not weakened: `fakeImage` records options, `openAi` records bodies and forwards options, `Setup.image` typed loosely. Checks: deno test (71 passed), jest (5350 passed, 2 skipped), lint, tsc, db reset, test db (1729 PASS). No real AI calls.

section: Moderation check before the photo call
title: Check the image prompt with OpenAI's free moderation endpoint before the image call
text: Check the image prompt with OpenAI's free moderation endpoint before the image call (spec 6.11), so a bad prompt stops with us instead of reaching `gpt-image-1-mini`: each `moderation_blocked` refusal there counts against our OpenAI account, and a moderation check doesn't. A new `generate-recipe-photo/moderation.ts`: `moderateText(text, options)` POSTs `{ model: 'omni-moderation-latest', input: text }` to `https://api.openai.com/v1/moderations` (a plain `fetch` with `OPENAI_API_KEY`, no SDK, as `image.ts`), with a 10 s timeout, and returns `{ flagged, categories }` (the names of the true categories, sorted); it follows `AI_IMAGE_MODEL` (`mock` answers not flagged with no network call; `off` never gets here). Failures throw `ModerationFailedError` (HTTP error, network error, timeout, an answer without `results[0].flagged`). `handler.ts`: right after `buildRecipePhotoImagePrompt(description)`, moderate that exact `imagePrompt` (a `moderate` dep, defaulting to `moderateText`, as `generateImage` is). Flagged: `fail({ code: 'not_food', by: 'moderation' }, …, 'moderation_flagged')`, so the reservation is released and the image model is never called. Moderation failed: fail closed with `generation_failed`, `step: 'moderation'`, never calling the image model. Add `'moderation'` to the `GenerateFailure` unions and make sure `request.ts` maps both to the same 422 / 502 as the existing cases. Log one `ai_calls` row per moderation call with task `recipePhotoModeration` (status `ok` with `output: { flagged, categories }`, `refused` when flagged, or the failure status; `fallback_of` the description row), the way the image row is written; check the `ai_calls` migrations, the admin portal's task lists and `admin_ai_calls` kinds accept the new task name and show it with the image rows, adding it where tasks are enumerated. Spec 6.11: add the moderation step between the description and Generate, change "moderation left at its default" to say the prompt is moderated by us first, and add a sentence to "Why no user text reaches the image model" that the check is there to keep refusals (account strikes) off our OpenAI account, not to catch anything the image model wouldn't. Deno tests (`moderation.test.ts`, `handler.test.ts`): the request body and URL; flagged and not flagged answers parsed; HTTP error, network error, timeout and a malformed answer each throw; `mock` makes no call; in the handler a flagged prompt is 422 `not_food` with the slot released and `generateImage` never called; a moderation failure is 502 with the slot released and no image call; a clean prompt goes on to the image as now; the moderated text is exactly the prompt sent to the image model; each case writes its `ai_calls` row. Trying it for real: `yarn ai:image` (`cli.ts`) prints each moderation answer (flagged and the categories) and gains `--description "<text>"`, which skips the description call and builds the image prompt from that text, so a flagged prompt can be tried against the real endpoint for free (it stops before the image); add it to `USAGE` and `cli.test.ts`, and reject it with `--title`, `--file` or a link. `yarn ai:eval:photo` (`eval/eval.ts`) also moderates the image prompt of every case described as food and counts a flagged one as a failure (a false positive would block a real recipe), printing the categories; the totals line shows how many were moderated and flagged. Add ordinary cases with edgy names to `eval/cases.json`, each expected food and not flagged: Blood orange salad, Bloody Mary, Drunken noodles, Devilled eggs, Spotted dick, Death by chocolate cake, Butchered chicken thighs with garlic, Hot and sour soup. With a mock model the eval skips moderation. Update `eval.test.ts` for the new check. Leave the run's results (flagged count, any case flagged) in progress.md; if any ordinary case is flagged, say so there and don't loosen the check.
notes: Moderation check before the photo call (2026-10-21, spec 6.11): DONE, checked off. New `generate-recipe-photo/moderation.ts`: `moderateText(text, options)` POSTs `{ model: 'omni-moderation-latest', input }` to `/v1/moderations` (plain fetch, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, 10 s timeout) and returns `{ flagged, categories }` (the true categories, sorted). It follows `AI_IMAGE_MODEL` (`mock`: not flagged, no call; `off` throws). `ModerationFailedError` (failure `api_error`/`timeout`/`invalid_output`/`error`, with HTTP status and body) covers HTTP, network, timeout and an answer without `results[0].flagged`; plus `moderationModelId`. `handler.ts`: a `moderate` dep (default `moderateText`) runs on the exact `imagePrompt` right after it's built. Flagged → `fail({ code: 'not_food', by: 'moderation' }, …, 'moderation_flagged')`; `ModerationFailedError` → `generation_failed`, `step: 'moderation'` (fails closed). The image model is never called in either case. `'moderation'` added to both `GenerateFailure` unions; `request.ts` already maps by code (422 / 502), no change. One `ai_calls` row per check, task `recipePhotoModeration` (new `RECIPE_PHOTO_MODERATION_TASK` in `run-ai-task.ts`): model `openai:omni-moderation-latest` or `mock`, the image prompt and its version, `ok` with output `{ flagged, categories }`, `refused` when flagged (same output, `error` "Flagged: …"), or the failure status with HTTP status/body; `fallback_of` is the description row (a `logStep` shared with the image row). Migration `20261126120000_ai_calls_moderation.sql`: `ai_call_stats` fallbacks and `admin_list_ai_calls` `recovered` leave out moderation rows as they do image rows (task is free text and `ai_call_flag` already flags `refused`, so nothing else was needed). Admin: `TASK_LABELS` gains "AI photo: moderation" (between description and image); `linkLabel` reads a moderation link as "Moderation" / "Description". CLI: prints each moderation answer (`formatModeration`). `--description "<text>"` skips the description call, builds the prompt from the cleaned text and moderates it: flagged stops before the image (exit 1), otherwise it makes the image. It's rejected with --title/--ingredients/--cuisine/--file/a link and with --describe-only, and is in USAGE. Eval: moderates the image prompt of every case described as food (needs OPENAI_API_KEY; exit 2 without it or with AI_IMAGE_MODEL=off). A flagged or failed check is a miss; each answer is printed, and the totals show `moderated:  N, M flagged`; the mock skips moderation. Eight edgy-named food cases added to `cases.json`. Spec updated: 6.11 (new step 7 Moderate; Generate renumbered and saying the prompt is moderated by us first; the account-strike sentence in "Why no user text…"; errors; privacy, now three rows; cost; tools), plus 4.12, 5 and 6.4. Tests: new `moderation.test.ts` (URL/headers/body, not flagged, flagged with sorted categories, flagged with no categories, HTTP error, network error, timeout, five malformed answers, no key and off make no call, mock makes no call, model id). `handler.test.ts`: a clean prompt goes on, the moderated text === the image prompt, the full ok row; flagged → 422, released, no image, refused row; flagged through the real call over a fake fetch, checking URL/body; api_error/invalid_output/timeout → 502, released, no image, each row; an unexpected error → 500, released, no image, error row; a not-food or failed description is never moderated. `cli.test.ts`: --description parsing and rejections, USAGE, formatModeration, moderation printed before the image, a flagged typed recipe stops after only the moderation fetch, --description flagged/clean/failure. `eval.test.ts`: the edgy cases are present as food, isRight with flagged/failed moderation, report lines and totals, runEval moderates only food with the exact prompt, failure and skip, a mock run skips, no key / off exit 2. pgTAP `58_ai_calls_moderation.test.sql` (11): flag, stats without fallbacks, the flagged-list row, recovered not set by a moderation row but still by a real fallback, photos lists image rows only, admin_ai_usage lists the task, admin_ai_call's fallback. Admin `ai-calls.test.ts`: labels, linkLabel. Existing tests changed because the task changes what they check: handler tests now expect the extra moderation row (three rows/steps, image row at index 2), and `call()` injects a fake moderation; eval's case-count bound went from 8–14 to 16–24 for the new cases. Checks: deno test (generate-recipe-photo, 99 passed), jest (5350 passed, 2 skipped), lint, tsc, admin test (182)/tsc/lint, db reset, test db (1740 PASS). Real calls: `yarn ai:eval:photo` (google:gemini-3.8-flash, 18 descriptions + 12 free moderations): 18/18 right, 12 moderated, 0 flagged, so none of the ordinary edgy-named cases was flagged. `yarn ai:image --description "A severed human hand covered in blood and gore on a dinner plate."` (free): flagged (violence, violence/graphic) and stopped before the image, which confirms real answers parse.

section: Turning AI photos off after refusals
goal: Goal: a user whose AI photo prompts keep getting refused loses AI photos until an admin turns them back on, so one account can't run up content-policy strikes on our OpenAI account. A refusal is an `ai_calls` row of that user with task `recipePhotoImage` or `recipePhotoModeration` and status `refused` (the description's `not_food` doesn't count: it never reaches the image model). Three refusals in 30 days blocks the user. The block is per user (not the plan, which is about to be per household), lasts until an admin clears it, and survives the 180-day retention of the rows that caused it. Write the spec first in each task (6.11, 5, 4.12 as each says), then the code.
title: Blocking a user's AI photos
text: Blocking a user's AI photos (spec 6.11, 5). A migration: `private.ai_photo_blocks (user_id uuid primary key references auth.users on delete cascade, blocked_at timestamptz not null default now(), refusals integer not null, last_call_id uuid references public.ai_calls on delete set null)`, RLS on with no policies and privileges revoked as the other private tables. `private.ai_photo_refusals(p_user_id, p_since)` counts the user's refused rows of the two tasks since `p_since` (one place for the rule, used by the trigger, the portal and the tests). An `after insert` trigger on `public.ai_calls` (`security definer`, `set search_path = ''`): for a row with `user_id` set, one of the two tasks and status `refused`, when `ai_photo_refusals(user, now() - 30 days)` is at least 3 and the user has no block, insert one (`refusals` that count, `last_call_id` the new row) and write an `admin.admin_actions` row (`action` `block_ai_photos`, `target_user_id`, `performed_by` null, `details` `{ refusals, window_days: 30 }`) so it shows in the portal's activity. Keep the threshold and window as constants at the top of the migration, named in the spec. `reserve_recipe_photo_ai` answers a new status `blocked` before anything else (no slot, no budget used) when the caller has a block. `handler.ts`: `ReserveResult` gains `blocked`, which throws `GeneratePhotoError({ code: 'ai_photos_blocked' })` ("AI photos are turned off for your account"); add it to `GenerateFailure` and make `request.ts` answer 403 for it. The app (`src/features/recipes/photo-upload.ts`): `ai_photos_blocked` is a new `PhotoGenerationError` whose toast is "AI photos are turned off for your account." (no Try again), and it calls `lostFeature('recipe_photo_ai')` as `not_entitled` does, so the Generate with AI row goes away until the features reload; strings in `en.ts` and `es.ts` ("Las fotos con IA están desactivadas para tu cuenta."). The Generate row stays shown for a blocked user until they try (the app isn't told about blocks up front). Spec 6.11: a paragraph on the rule (what counts, 3 in 30 days, until an admin clears it, `blocked` checked first); 5: the table; 4.5's failure list: the new toast. pgTAP (new `57_ai_photo_blocks.test.sql`): two refusals don't block, the third does, once, with its audit row; `not_food` description rows, other statuses, other tasks and refusals older than 30 days don't count; a null `user_id` row does nothing; a blocked user's `reserve_recipe_photo_ai` answers `blocked` with no slot taken and no usage counted; deleting the user deletes the block. Deno (`handler.test.ts`, `request.test.ts`): `blocked` is 403 `ai_photos_blocked` and calls no model. Jest: the toast and the dropped feature.
notes: Blocking a user's AI photos (2026-10-21, spec 6.11, 5): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261127120000_ai_photo_blocks.sql`: the rule's numbers as `private.ai_photo_block_threshold()` (3) and `private.ai_photo_block_window()` (30 days) at the top; `private.ai_photo_blocks` (RLS on, no policies, privileges revoked); `private.ai_photo_refusals(user, since)` (refused `recipePhotoModeration`/`recipePhotoImage` rows); an `after insert` trigger on `ai_calls` (`private.block_ai_photos_on_refusal`, security definer, a per-user advisory lock so concurrent refusals can't both miss) that blocks once at 3 and writes `admin.admin_actions` (`block_ai_photos`, performed_by null, `{ refusals, window_days: 30 }`); `admin.admin_actions.performed_by` made nullable for that row (keeps its default); `reserve_recipe_photo_ai` answers `blocked` first. Function: `ReserveResult`/store accept `blocked` → `GeneratePhotoError({ code: 'ai_photos_blocked' })` → 403 in `request.ts`; `ai_photos_blocked` added to the shared error codes (schema test updated, since the task changes what it lists) and index.ts's header. App: `photo-upload.ts` maps the code to a new `ai_photos_blocked` error, toast "AI photos are turned off for your account." (no Try again) and `lostFeature('recipe_photo_ai')`; strings in en/es, ran `yarn i18n:export`. Spec 4.5 (toast), 5 (table, reserve's `blocked`), 6.11 (step 4, errors, a "Blocking a user's AI photos" paragraph). Tests: pgTAP `57_ai_photo_blocks.test.sql` (24: access, constants, two don't block, the third does with last_call_id and one audit row by nobody, a fourth changes nothing, not_food descriptions/other statuses/other tasks/old rows don't count, null user does nothing, image-only refusals block, blocked reserve takes no slot and no usage and comes before not_found, an unblocked user still reserves, user deletion deletes the block but keeps the audit, deleting the call nulls last_call_id); Deno `handler.test.ts` (blocked: 403, no description, moderation or image call, no release) and new `request.test.ts` (blocked 403 with message, every failure's status/code, 200); Jest `recipe-photo-sheet.test.tsx` (blocked toast without Try again, lostFeature called and the Generate row gone from the sheet; a bare 403 still reads as not_entitled; the message in en and es). Checks: deno test (103 passed), jest (5352 passed, 2 skipped), lint, tsc, db reset, test db (PASS). No real AI calls.

title: Seeing and clearing blocks in the portal
text: Seeing and clearing blocks in the portal (spec 4.12 Users, Flagged AI calls). A migration: `admin_user_detail` gains `ai_photo_block` (null, or `{ blocked_at, refusals, last_call_id }`) and `ai_photo_refusals_30d` (from `private.ai_photo_refusals`); `admin_list_users` gains `ai_photos_blocked boolean` and an optional `p_blocked boolean` filter; `admin_unblock_ai_photos(p_user_id, p_note)` (`private.require_admin()`, the note required as for a plan change, `not blocked` `P0002` when there's none) deletes the block and audits `unblock_ai_photos` with the note and `details` `{ refusals, blocked_at }`. Unblocking starts the count over: the trigger only counts refusals after the latest `unblock_ai_photos` for that user (or 30 days, whichever is later), so the old refusals don't block them again on the next one; put that in `private.ai_photo_refusals` and cover it in the first task's test file. Portal (`admin/`, follow `admin/AGENTS.md`): on the user page (`admin/app/(portal)/users/[id]/page.tsx`) an **AI photos** card: when blocked, "Blocked since <date> after <n> refused prompts" in `danger`, a link to the refusals (the AI calls page filtered by this user and flag `refused`; check the filter takes both tasks) and an **Unblock** form with a required note, modelled on `ChangePlan` and `plan-actions.ts`; when not, "Not blocked", with "<n> refused prompts in the last 30 days (blocks at 3)" when n > 0. The Users list shows a `danger` "AI photos blocked" badge on blocked users and gains a Blocked filter. Activity names both actions ("Blocked AI photos (3 refusals)", "Unblocked AI photos"), the block's admin shown as "Automatic". The AI calls page's `refused` rows of a blocked user show the badge too. Update `admin/lib/types.ts`, `src/constants/__tests__/admin-drift.test.ts` if it covers these, and `docs/admin.md` (how blocks work, unblocking, and a SQL snippet listing blocked users). Spec 4.12: the AI photos card, the badge, the filter and the two activity actions. pgTAP (`50_admin_users` or the new block test): non-admins refused; detail and list show the block; unblock deletes it, audits with the note, needs a note and fails on a user with none; after an unblock, two new refusals don't block and a third does. Portal tests (`yarn --cwd admin test`), lint and `tsc --noEmit`.
notes: Seeing and clearing blocks in the portal (2026-10-21, spec 4.12, 6.11): DONE, checked off. section: Turning AI photos off after refusals
goal: Goal: a user whose AI photo prompts keep getting refused loses AI photos until an admin turns them back on, so one account can't run up content-policy strikes on our OpenAI account. A refusal is an `ai_calls` row of that user with task `recipePhotoImage` or `recipePhotoModeration` and status `refused` (the description's `not_food` doesn't count: it never reaches the image model). Three refusals in 30 days blocks the user. The block is per user (not the plan, which is about to be per household), lasts until an admin clears it, and survives the 180-day retention of the rows that caused it. Write the spec first in each task (6.11, 5, 4.12 as each says), then the code.
title: A way to test blocks by hand
text: A way to test blocks by hand (spec 6.11 Testing blocks). Two tools, both local only. **Fake refusals in the database:** `scripts/ai-refusals.ts`, run as `yarn dev:ai-refusals <email> [count]` (default 3) and `yarn dev:ai-refusals <email> --clear`, connects to the local database (`postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:55322/postgres`, overridable with `DATABASE_URL`) and refuses to run when the host isn't `127.0.0.1` or `localhost`, so it can't touch hosted. It looks the user up by email (an error naming the email when there's none) and inserts `count` `ai_calls` rows for them: task `recipePhotoImage`, status `refused`, model `mock`, `user_id` and their oldest household, `error` "Fake refusal (dev:ai-refusals)", `created_at` now. The rows go through the real trigger, so the third one blocks the user exactly as a real refusal would; it prints the user's refusal count and whether they're blocked. `--clear` deletes that user's fake rows (matched by the `error` text), their block and the block's `block_ai_photos` audit row, leaving them as before. **A refusal from the mock model:** with `AI_IMAGE_MODEL=mock`, `generateImage` throws `ImageRefusedError('Refused: moderation_blocked (mock)')` when the image prompt contains `refuse-me` (the mock moderation check answers flagged for the same word once the moderation task is in), so a recipe named "refuse-me pasta" makes a real refused row through the whole function and the app. Since the description model rewrites the title, check the word reaches the prompt; if it doesn't, key the mock refusal off the recipe's title in the handler instead (mock only). Add the script to `package.json`, `docs/admin.md` (a "Testing AI photo blocks" section: the script, the mock word, and for hosted a SQL snippet the user runs in the SQL editor that inserts the same three rows for an email and one that clears them) and `manual-checks.md`: (1) `yarn dev:ai-refusals <you> 2`, the portal's user page shows "2 refused prompts in the last 30 days (blocks at 3)" and not blocked; (2) once more with 1, the page shows Blocked with the date and 3, the Users list shows the badge and the Blocked filter finds them, Activity shows "Blocked AI photos (3 refusals)" by Automatic; (3) in the app, Generate with AI on a recipe with no photo shows "AI photos are turned off for your account." and the row goes away; (4) Unblock in the portal with a note, Activity shows it, the app can generate again after the features reload; (5) with the mock model, three recipes named "refuse-me …" each get "Couldn't make a photo for this recipe" and the third blocks the account; (6) `--clear` puts everything back. Deno tests: the mock refuses on the word and makes a photo otherwise; the script's host check refuses a non-local URL (export the check and test it alone).

New `scripts/ai-refusals.ts` (`yarn dev:ai-refusals <email> [count] | --clear`, Deno, runs `psql` with `-v` variables): exported `assertLocalDatabase` (postgres URL on 127.0.0.1/localhost only) and `parseArgs` (count 1–100, default 3); looks the user up by email (error naming it), inserts one `ai_calls` row per statement (`recipePhotoImage`, `refused`, `mock`, oldest household, error "Fake refusal (dev:ai-refusals)") through the real trigger, prints the count and blocked/not blocked; `--clear` deletes the block's `block_ai_photos` audit row (created at/after `blocked_at`), the block and the fake rows. Ran it against local (2, 1 → blocked at 3; `--clear` → 0, not blocked; first attempt misreported "not blocked" because `boolean::text` is `true` not `t`, fixed). Mock refusal word: the mock description never repeats the title, so the word doesn't reach the prompt on its own; `image.ts` exports `MOCK_REFUSAL_WORD`/`hasMockRefusalWord` and the mock image model throws `ImageRefusedError('Refused: moderation_blocked (mock)')` on it, the mock `moderateText` answers `{ flagged: true, categories: ['mock'] }` on it, and the handler (mock image model only) appends ` (refuse-me)` to the description inside the image prompt when the title has the word, so through the function it's a refused moderation row. `package.json`: the script, and `<rootDir>/scripts/` in jest's `testPathIgnorePatterns` (scripts are Deno). Docs: `docs/admin.md` "Testing AI photo blocks" (script, mock word, hosted insert/clear SQL snippets), a "Testing blocks" paragraph in spec 6.11. Tests: `scripts/ai-refusals.test.ts` (host check accepts local, refuses hosted/LAN/lookalike hosts and non-postgres URLs; args); image.test.ts (mock refuses on the word in any case, photo otherwise; a real model sends it on); moderation.test.ts (mock flags on the word; real model unaffected); handler.test.ts (mock title → refused moderation row, not_food, released; past moderation → refused image row; no word → photo, prompt unchanged; real image model never sees the title). goal: Goal: a plan belongs to a household, not a user, and covers only the two AI features that cost real money: **recipe import** (link and photo, one allowance; the tags and step match an import makes are part of it) and **AI photos**. Everyone in a household gets its plan and shares its monthly allowance, so inviting people doesn't multiply it. Everything else the AI does is for everyone on every plan with no monthly limit: **categorize** (it fills the global catalog, so it helps everyone, and nobody gains from overusing it), **step matching** for recipes typed or edited by hand, and **Suggest tags**. Those keep per-user per-minute limits and gain per-user daily ceilings, which stop a scripted account rather than a person. Every number (the plans' monthly limits and the per-minute and daily ceilings) is a table row an admin edits in the portal, never a constant in code. Decisions behind it, for the spec task to write down: - **Feature keys** become two: `recipe_import` (link import and photo import alike; `recipe_import_photo` folds into it) and `recipe_photo_ai`. `categorize`, `step_ingredients` and `recipe_tags` stop being plan features. The import rule (an import needs `categorize`, `plan_features_import_needs_categorize`) goes away with them. - **Plans**, renamed so the names say what they are: **founding** ("Founding", replacing plus: `recipe_import` 50 a month, `recipe_photo_ai` 20 a month; the default until paid plans launch), **unlimited** (both, no monthly limit), **free** ("Free", replacing none: neither, though categorize, step matching and Suggest tags still work). **basic** is deleted (it had only categorize and step matching, which everyone now has); a household on it moves to free. The ids change too (they're referenced by `household_plans` and the audit log, so this is the last cheap moment): plus becomes `founding` and none becomes `free`; old audit rows keep the old ids as written. A household's first 30 days (`households.created_at`) get twice its plan's monthly limits, as now. - **Every household has an explicit plan.** A household's plan is its `household_plans` row and nothing else; there's no "unassigned, so the default". Creating a household (`create_household`, `private.create_personal_household`) writes its row with the plan that is the default at that moment, and the migration gives every existing household one. "Default" only means the plan new households start on: changing it never moves an existing household. A household with no row (which shouldn't exist) has no features. In the portal a household's plan can be changed to another plan but not cleared. - **Founding households** (every household made before paid plans launch) stay on founding, free of charge, for good, through their explicit rows. Until paid plans launch, new features may be added to founding; after that, founding is frozen: a new feature goes into a new plan, never into founding, so founders get only what founding had at launch. Changing founding's limits is allowed and applies to founders. `docs/admin.md` gets a "Launching paid plans" section: create the paid plan (its own name) and make it the default (new households only); existing households keep founding; never add a feature to founding. - **One household per new user.** `create_household` refuses (`already in a household`, `P0001`) when the caller is already a member of any household, so a user can't make extra households to multiply allowances. The app only ever creates one when the user has none (`ensureStarterData` at sign-up, Start my own list), and the server makes one when a user leaves their only household. Leaving your only household (deleting it, as its last member) and getting a fresh one with a fresh allowance and first month is allowed: it costs every list and recipe, so it isn't worth farming. - **Safety limits**, per user, the same on every plan, in a table (below). Seeded: categorize 60 requests a minute and 500 LLM-bound names a day; step matching 30 a minute and 100 a day; Suggest tags 20 a minute and 50 a day; link import 10 a minute; photo import 5 a minute; recipe imports (link and photo together) 100 a day; AI photos 40 a day. Founding can't reach the last two (its first month allows 100 imports and 40 photos in the whole month); they bound plans with no monthly limit. Null means no limit. A per-minute refusal is 429 `rate_limited` as now; a daily one is a new **429 `daily_limit`** with `resets_at` (the next UTC midnight). In the app: categorize leaves names `pending` for the catch-up, step matching stops for the session, and the import sheet, photo import, Suggest tags and AI photos say "You've reached today's limit. Try again tomorrow." ("Llegaste al límite de hoy. Inténtalo mañana."). Only two live users, both on unlimited: no edge cases for existing assignments, and this month's usage isn't carried over (household counting starts at the migration). Old app builds must keep working until the last task: a request with no household falls back as each task says, and `my_features` keeps answering the old feature keys. Never deploy to hosted Supabase: leave the commands in progress.md.
title: Spec
text: Spec. Rewrite `docs/spec.md` for this section's decisions before any code, and keep it in step if a later task changes a detail. 4.12: Plans and features (the two feature keys, the three seeded plans, the import rule removed, the plan renames, the freeze rule for founding after paid launch and why), Per household (explicit rows, what "default" means, founding households, one household per new user), Monthly limits (the new seeds; categorize, step matching and tags have none; the first month by household age only, so `private.user_first_month_ends_at` and `private.categorize_monthly_limit` aren't needed), a new **Safety limits** part (the table, the seeds, `rate_limited` versus `daily_limit`, what the app does with each), Checking, Changing a household's plan (no clearing), Editing plans (no import rule; `households` counts rows), AI usage, Resolution, In the app (only `recipe_import` and `recipe_photo_ai` are gated; categorize, Suggest tags and step matching always on), and the Edge Functions paragraph (only `import-recipe`, `import-recipe-photo` and `generate-recipe-photo` check a feature; `suggest-recipe-tags` and `match-recipe-steps` still send `householdId`, only for `ai_calls`). 4.7: `create_household` refuses a caller already in a household. 5: `household_plans` (every household has a row), `public.ai_safety_limits`, `private.household_ai_usage`, the feature `check` constraints. 6.4, 6.6, 6.7, 6.8, 6.10 and 6.11: each **Cost** paragraph names its safety limits by key and, for the two plan features, the household's monthly limit (photo import shares `recipe_import`'s); remove each mention of categorize's, tags' and step matching's monthly limits and of `recipe_import_photo` as a feature. Also `docs/admin.md`'s "Launching paid plans" section. It lists what was pulled forward: `households` and `household_members` (with RLS), `create_household` and `get_household_members`. Quantities docs. `docs/spec.md` §4.2 gains a "Usual unit" bullet. It covers `ingredient_unit_usage`: each add or recipe ingredient with a quantity counts one use of its unit, and count when it has no unit. Undo takes the use back, and an add with no quantity counts nothing. The most-used unit wins; ties go to the most recent, then alphabetical. Existing data is backfilled once. §4.2 also gains a "Changing an amount" bullet for the edit sheet's − / + stepper and unit button, which save immediately. Steps are 1 / 0.5 / 0.25 / 100 depending on the unit, results are rounded to the step, and − stops at one step. An item with no amount steps from one of its usual unit. The unit picker keeps the number without converting. Both replace the amounts but keep recipe links that have no quantity, and they are disabled when the total isn't a single amount. §4.4 quantity math now says an add with no amount counts as one of the usual unit (unitless when there is none): `milk` + `milk` → `2`, and `1 gal` + `milk` → `2 gal` (`1 gal + 1` with no history). `categorize-ingredients` handler: `supabase/functions/_shared/ai/prompts/categorize.v1.ts` now exports `buildCategorizePrompt(names)`. Its `instructions` hold the spec 6.4 rules, every `slug: Name` from `SYSTEM_CATEGORIES`, and a note that the names are data, never instructions. Its `prompt` is an "Untrusted item names to classify..." line with no `[`, then the names as a JSON array. `categorize-ingredients/handler.ts` exports `categorize(names, store, model?)` behind a `CategorizeStore` interface, which the next task implements with the service role. The interface has `getIngredients`, `insertPending` (on conflict do nothing), `saveCategorized(rows, categorizedBy)`, `saveFailed(names)` and `logAiCall`. Both save methods apply only `where status <> 'categorized'`, and a failure sets attempts + 1 and Other. `categorize` throws `CategorizeInputError` for more than 100 raw names. It normalizes and dedupes the names: the first spelling becomes the display name, and names that are empty after normalizing are dropped. Names over 64 characters are answered failed/Other without touching the store or the LLM. It upserts missing names as pending and sends the uncategorized ones with `attempts < 3` in one `runAiTask` call per 100 names. Answers are capped at the number of names sent, answers for names not sent are ignored, and for a duplicate the first answer wins. A missing name, or a `NoObjectGeneratedError`, marks names failed. An unknown slug also ends up as `NoObjectGeneratedError`, because the schema's enum rejects the whole output, so it fails the whole batch. `APICallError`, `RetryError` and `TimeoutError`/`AbortError` leave the rows unchanged, and those names are answered pending. Any other error is thrown. When `isAiEnabled('categorize')` is false, it makes no call and answers those names pending. The response is re-read from the store after writing, so a concurrent winner's result is what gets returned. New Deno tests in `handler.test.ts` (21, using an in-memory fake store and `MockLanguageModelV4`): all-known input makes zero calls. 8 unknown + 4 known make one call with exactly the 8, `categorized_by = test:model` and one `ai_calls` record. A categorized name isn't sent again. Names are normalized and deduped, and empty ones are dropped. A missing name becomes failed/Other with attempts 1. An unknown slug fails the whole batch (`invalid_output`). A schema failure increments attempts (0→1, 1→2). An answer for a name not sent is ignored, and for a duplicate answer the first wins. Drag to reorder in As added moves rows live (2026-10-16, spec 4.6): the cause was each row's `onLayout` doing `boxes.set({ ...boxes.get(), [id]: box })` on the JS thread. In Reanimated 4.5 a JS-thread `set` is only scheduled onto the UI thread while `get` reads the UI value now, so rows laying out together overwrote one another and only the last row's box survived. The rest counted as zero height, so nothing made room and the drop slots were wrong. Fix: `boxes.modify(all => withBox(all, id, box))`, which runs in order on the UI thread. Also pulled the drag reaction's math into a pure `dragTo(rows, from, translation, scrolled)` in `row-drag.ts`, placed below `clampDrag` because the worklets plugin turns worklet functions into consts, which aren't hoisted. Tests: `row-drag.test.ts` adds `dragTo` (down and up past several rows including a taller one, across an auto-scroll both ways, clamped at the ends, no boxes) and `withBox`. `reorderable-rows.test.tsx`'s Reanimated mock now defers JS-thread `set`/`modify` until the UI thread runs, as on device (an existing test file's mock changed, no assertions weakened), and adds two tests that the other rows make room live, down and up. Push tokens and notification settings (2026-10-17, spec 4.13, 5). New migration supabase/migrations/20261103120000_push_notifications.sql. public.push_tokens (token pk, user_id cascade + index, platform ios|android, created_at/updated_at with the set_updated_at trigger) has RLS on and no client grants. register_push_token(p_token, p_platform) and unregister_push_token(p_token) are security definer, granted to authenticated only, and raise `not signed in` (42501) without a user. register checks the shape `^(Exponent|Expo)PushToken\[[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\]$` and ≤ 200 chars (`invalid token`, 22023) and the platform (`invalid platform`), then upserts on token: another user's token moves to the caller and updated_at is bumped. unregister deletes only the caller's row and is a no-op otherwise. public.notification_settings (user_id pk cascade, items_added/shopping default true, quiet_hours_start/end, time_zone default 'UTC') checks the quiet hours are both null or both set and different, has a trigger (private.check_notification_time_zone) raising `invalid time zone` (22023) for a name not in pg_timezone_names, and select/insert/update own-row policies (no delete). private.push_recipients(household, actor, kind, at) returns (user_id, token, platform), one row per device, for current members other than the actor, with the kind on (`items_added` | `shopping`, else `invalid kind`) and outside quiet hours [start, end) in their own time zone (start > end wraps midnight); a missing settings row is the defaults. Execute is service_role only; the migration grants service_role usage on schema private. Note for the worker task: `private` isn't exposed by PostgREST (config.toml schemas = public, graphql_public), so supabase-js `.rpc` can't reach push_recipients as is; the worker needs a direct Postgres connection or a public service_role-only wrapper.
