goal: Goal: a plan belongs to a household, not a user, and covers only the two AI features that cost real money: **recipe import** (link and photo, one allowance; the tags and step match an import makes are part of it) and **AI photos**. Everyone in a household gets its plan and shares its monthly allowance, so inviting people doesn't multiply it. Everything else the AI does is for everyone on every plan with no monthly limit: **categorize** (it fills the global catalog, so it helps everyone, and nobody gains from overusing it), **step matching** for recipes typed or edited by hand, and **Suggest tags**. Those keep per-user per-minute limits and gain per-user daily ceilings, which stop a scripted account rather than a person. Every number (the plans' monthly limits and the per-minute and daily ceilings) is a table row an admin edits in the portal, never a constant in code. Decisions behind it, for the spec task to write down: - **Feature keys** become two: `recipe_import` (link import and photo import alike; `recipe_import_photo` folds into it) and `recipe_photo_ai`. `categorize`, `step_ingredients` and `recipe_tags` stop being plan features. The import rule (an import needs `categorize`, `plan_features_import_needs_categorize`) goes away with them. - **Plans**, renamed so the names say what they are: **founding** ("Founding", replacing plus: `recipe_import` 50 a month, `recipe_photo_ai` 20 a month; the default until paid plans launch), **unlimited** (both, no monthly limit), **free** ("Free", replacing none: neither, though categorize, step matching and Suggest tags still work). **basic** is deleted (it had only categorize and step matching, which everyone now has); a household on it moves to free. The ids change too (they're referenced by `household_plans` and the audit log, so this is the last cheap moment): plus becomes `founding` and none becomes `free`; old audit rows keep the old ids as written. A household's first 30 days (`households.created_at`) get twice its plan's monthly limits, as now. - **Every household has an explicit plan.** A household's plan is its `household_plans` row and nothing else; there's no "unassigned, so the default". Creating a household (`create_household`, `private.create_personal_household`) writes its row with the plan that is the default at that moment, and the migration gives every existing household one. "Default" only means the plan new households start on: changing it never moves an existing household. A household with no row (which shouldn't exist) has no features. In the portal a household's plan can be changed to another plan but not cleared. - **Founding households** (every household made before paid plans launch) stay on founding, free of charge, for good, through their explicit rows. Until paid plans launch, new features may be added to founding; after that, founding is frozen: a new feature goes into a new plan, never into founding, so founders get only what founding had at launch. Changing founding's limits is allowed and applies to founders. `docs/admin.md` gets a "Launching paid plans" section: create the paid plan (its own name) and make it the default (new households only); existing households keep founding; never add a feature to founding. - **One household per new user.** `create_household` refuses (`already in a household`, `P0001`) when the caller is already a member of any household, so a user can't make extra households to multiply allowances. The app only ever creates one when the user has none (`ensureStarterData` at sign-up, Start my own list), and the server makes one when a user leaves their only household. Leaving your only household (deleting it, as its last member) and getting a fresh one with a fresh allowance and first month is allowed: it costs every list and recipe, so it isn't worth farming. - **Safety limits**, per user, the same on every plan, in a table (below). Seeded: categorize 60 requests a minute and 500 LLM-bound names a day; step matching 30 a minute and 100 a day; Suggest tags 20 a minute and 50 a day; link import 10 a minute; photo import 5 a minute; recipe imports (link and photo together) 100 a day; AI photos 40 a day. Founding can't reach the last two (its first month allows 100 imports and 40 photos in the whole month); they bound plans with no monthly limit. Null means no limit. A per-minute refusal is 429 `rate_limited` as now; a daily one is a new **429 `daily_limit`** with `resets_at` (the next UTC midnight). In the app: categorize leaves names `pending` for the catch-up, step matching stops for the session, and the import sheet, photo import, Suggest tags and AI photos say "You've reached today's limit. Try again tomorrow." ("Llegaste al límite de hoy. Inténtalo mañana."). Only two live users, both on unlimited: no edge cases for existing assignments, and this month's usage isn't carried over (household counting starts at the migration). Old app builds must keep working until the last task: a request with no household falls back as each task says, and `my_features` keeps answering the old feature keys. Never deploy to hosted Supabase: leave the commands in progress.md.
title: Household plans, the two feature keys and resolution
text: Household plans, the two feature keys and resolution (spec 4.12, 4.7, 5). A new migration: `public.household_plans (household_id uuid primary key references households on delete cascade, plan_id text not null references plans, assigned_at timestamptz not null default now())`, an index on `plan_id`, RLS on with no policies and privileges revoked as `user_plans`, the `before update` trigger setting `assigned_at` (`private.set_assigned_at`). Rows for every household: an owner's `user_plans` plan (when two owners' plans meet, the plan with more features wins; ties by plan id), else the current default; every household of jgpasch@gmail.com on unlimited. `create_household` and `private.create_personal_household` insert the new household's row with the default plan (no row when no plan is the default), and `create_household` raises `already in a household` (`P0001`) when the caller is a member of any household. Check what the device does when the push's `create_household` is refused (`src/sync/push.ts` records and skips a 4xx): the local household must not linger, so make the next pull purge it if it doesn't already, and test it. Feature keys: `plan_features` and `plan_limits` `check` constraints and `private.feature_keys()` become `recipe_import`, `recipe_photo_ai`; a plan with `recipe_import_photo` keeps (or gains) `recipe_import`; delete the `categorize`, `step_ingredients`, `recipe_tags` and `recipe_import_photo` rows; drop the `plan_features_import_needs_categorize` trigger. Plans: create `founding` ("Founding", the default, `recipe_import` 50 and `recipe_photo_ai` 20) and `free` ("Free", no features), move every `user_plans` row on plus to founding and on none or basic to free (kept until the last task), then delete plus, none and basic; unlimited gets null for both. Do the renames before writing the `household_plans` rows, so no row ever names an old id. Grep `supabase/tests/`, `supabase/functions/`, `admin/` (not `node_modules`), `src/` and `docs/admin.md` for `plus`, `none` and `basic` used as plan ids or names and update them (an SF Symbol named `plus` isn't one). `has_feature(user, feature, household)`: false unless the user is a member of `household`, then whether its plan has the feature; `household` null (an old client) takes the best of the user's households (any of them has it). `private.first_month_ends_at(household)` (`households.created_at` + 30 days) and `private.monthly_limit(feature, household)` (the household's plan, doubled in its first month); keep the old `private.monthly_limit(user, feature, household)` as a wrapper for the `check_*_limit` callers until the usage task, resolving the household as `has_feature` does. `public.my_household_features()` (authenticated, `security definer`): `{ households: { <household id>: [features sorted, "C" collation] } }` for every household the caller is in. `my_features(household)` keeps answering old builds in the old keys: always `categorize`, `recipe_tags` and `step_ingredients`, plus `recipe_import` and `recipe_import_photo` when any of the user's households has `recipe_import`, plus `recipe_photo_ai` likewise. `categorize-ingredients`, `suggest-recipe-tags` and `match-recipe-steps` stop calling `requireFeature`; `import-recipe-photo` checks `recipe_import`. `supabase/seed.sql`: make `unlimited` the default plan instead of assigning the dev user (their households are made on the device after the seed, so they get unlimited rows). pgTAP (extend `17_plans.test.sql`, `48_plan_limits.test.sql`, the household tests): a new household gets the default's row and keeps it when the default changes; a second `create_household` is refused and a user with none can make one; leaving your only household makes one with a row; the migration's rows (owner's plan, a member's not, the default otherwise, basic and none to free, plus to founding; the old ids are gone); a household's row decides its features, no row none, a non-member false, a null household the best of the user's; first month doubles; `my_household_features` and `my_features`' legacy answer; the old keys are refused by the `check` constraints; deleting a household deletes its row. Deno tests: the three functions that no longer check a feature answer a user on none.
notes: Household plans, the two feature keys and resolution (2026-10-21, spec 4.12, 4.7, 5): DONE, checked off.
manualChecks: Household plans, the two feature keys and resolution: (1) the migration's backfill on hosted-like data, following the steps at the top of `.migration-check-before.sql` (reset to 20261128120000, load the file with psql, `supabase migration up --local`, compare the households' plans with the expected list there), then `supabase db reset` and delete `.migration-check-before.sql`. (2) On a development build signed in as a user who already has a household on the server, get the device to make its own starter household (e.g. sign in on a fresh install while offline, so `ensureStarterData` makes one, then go online): the push's `create_household` is refused (`already in a household`), and the next full pull (foreground the app) removes that household and its lists from the device, leaving the server's.

title: Safety limits in a table
text: Safety limits in a table (spec 4.12 Safety limits; 5; 6.4 to 6.11 Cost). A migration: `public.ai_safety_limits (key text primary key check (key in ('categorize', 'step_match', 'recipe_tags', 'recipe_import_link', 'recipe_import_photo', 'recipe_import', 'recipe_photo_ai')), per_minute integer check (per_minute >= 0), per_day integer check (per_day >= 0))`, RLS on with no policies and privileges revoked as `plan_limits`, seeded: `categorize` 60 / 500 (requests a minute, LLM-bound names a day), `step_match` 30 / 100, `recipe_tags` 20 / 50, `recipe_import_link` 10 / null, `recipe_import_photo` 5 / null, `recipe_import` null / 100 (link and photo imports together), `recipe_photo_ai` null / 40; null is no limit. `private.safety_limit(key)` reads it. Every `check_*_limit` function and `reserve_recipe_photo_ai` reads its per-minute and daily numbers from there instead of the hard-coded ones, the daily check summing that user's UTC day on the per-user usage tables (both import tables for `recipe_import`), and answers the new `daily_limit` (after `user_limit`, before the monthly check; nothing counted). Keep `reserve_recipe_photo_ai`'s `blocked` answer (the AI photo blocks) first, before any limit check. `check_categorize_limit`, `check_recipe_tags_limit` and `check_step_match_limit` drop their monthly check. The functions answer `daily_limit` as 429 `{ error: 'daily_limit', message, resets_at }` (the next UTC midnight, ISO 8601), in each function's error mapping and its shared error schema; categorize answers the names `pending` as for `rate_limited`. The app (`src/features/recipes/import.ts`, the photo import, `suggest-tags.ts`, the AI photo call, `ensure-step-match.ts`, categorize): `daily_limit` shows "You've reached today's limit. Try again tomorrow." where a user started the request, stops step matching for the session, and leaves categorize names pending; strings in `en.ts` and `es.ts` ("Llegaste al límite de hoy. Inténtalo mañana."). Portal (`admin/`, follow `admin/AGENTS.md`): `admin_list_safety_limits()` (read-only) and `admin_set_safety_limit(p_key, p_per_minute, p_per_day, p_note)` (`private.require_admin()`, note required as for plans, `unknown key` `P0002`, audited `set_safety_limit` with `details` `{ before, after }`); a **Safety limits** card on the Plans page listing each key with its two numbers (blank for none), its unit ("names a day" for categorize's daily, "requests a minute" and so on) and an edit form with the required note; Activity names the action. Update `admin/lib/types.ts`, `src/constants/__tests__/admin-drift.test.ts` if it covers these, and `docs/admin.md` (the card, and a SQL snippet for the Table Editor). pgTAP: each check's per-minute and daily refusals follow a changed row on the next call and count nothing; null skips the check; link and photo imports share the daily `recipe_import` count; categorize, tags and step matching have no monthly refusal; the admin functions refuse non-admins, need a note and audit. Deno: each function maps `daily_limit` to 429 with `resets_at`. Jest: the app's message and the session stop. Portal tests (`yarn --cwd admin test`), lint and `tsc --noEmit`.
notes: Safety limits in a table (spec 4.12 Safety limits). Migration `20261130120000_ai_safety_limits.sql`: `public.ai_safety_limits` (seeded as the spec's table, RLS on, no client privileges), `private.safety_limit(key)` and `private.safety_limit_keys()`; every `check_*_limit` and `reserve_recipe_photo_ai` read their numbers from it on each call and answer `user_limit` → `daily_limit` → `monthly_limit`, counting nothing on a refusal (null skips a check); categorize, tags and step matching lost their monthly check; link and photo imports share `recipe_import`'s daily (and, when set, per-minute) count via `private.recipe_import_safety`, under one per-user lock; `recipe_photo_ai_usage` gained a minute window, and `reserve_recipe_photo_ai` keeps `blocked` first (then not_found, already_generated, the safety limits, the month). Portal RPCs `admin_list_safety_limits()` and `admin_set_safety_limit(...)` (require_admin, note required, `unknown key` P0002, audited `set_safety_limit` with `{ before, after }`).

goal: Goal: a plan belongs to a household, not a user, and covers only the two AI features that cost real money: **recipe import** (link and photo, one allowance; the tags and step match an import makes are part of it) and **AI photos**. Everyone in a household gets its plan and shares its monthly allowance, so inviting people doesn't multiply it. Everything else the AI does is for everyone on every plan with no monthly limit: **categorize** (it fills the global catalog, so it helps everyone, and nobody gains from overusing it), **step matching** for recipes typed or edited by hand, and **Suggest tags**. Those keep per-user per-minute limits and gain per-user daily ceilings, which stop a scripted account rather than a person. Every number (the plans' monthly limits and the per-minute and daily ceilings) is a table row an admin edits in the portal, never a constant in code. Decisions behind it, for the spec task to write down: - **Feature keys** become two: `recipe_import` (link import and photo import alike; `recipe_import_photo` folds into it) and `recipe_photo_ai`. `categorize`, `step_ingredients` and `recipe_tags` stop being plan features. The import rule (an import needs `categorize`, `plan_features_import_needs_categorize`) goes away with them. - **Plans**, renamed so the names say what they are: **founding** ("Founding", replacing plus: `recipe_import` 50 a month, `recipe_photo_ai` 20 a month; the default until paid plans launch), **unlimited** (both, no monthly limit), **free** ("Free", replacing none: neither, though categorize, step matching and Suggest tags still work). **basic** is deleted (it had only categorize and step matching, which everyone now has); a household on it moves to free. The ids change too (they're referenced by `household_plans` and the audit log, so this is the last cheap moment): plus becomes `founding` and none becomes `free`; old audit rows keep the old ids as written. A household's first 30 days (`households.created_at`) get twice its plan's monthly limits, as now. - **Every household has an explicit plan.** A household's plan is its `household_plans` row and nothing else; there's no "unassigned, so the default". Creating a household (`create_household`, `private.create_personal_household`) writes its row with the plan that is the default at that moment, and the migration gives every existing household one. "Default" only means the plan new households start on: changing it never moves an existing household. A household with no row (which shouldn't exist) has no features. In the portal a household's plan can be changed to another plan but not cleared. - **Founding households** (every household made before paid plans launch) stay on founding, free of charge, for good, through their explicit rows. Until paid plans launch, new features may be added to founding; after that, founding is frozen: a new feature goes into a new plan, never into founding, so founders get only what founding had at launch. Changing founding's limits is allowed and applies to founders. `docs/admin.md` gets a "Launching paid plans" section: create the paid plan (its own name) and make it the default (new households only); existing households keep founding; never add a feature to founding. - **One household per new user.** `create_household` refuses (`already in a household`, `P0001`) when the caller is already a member of any household, so a user can't make extra households to multiply allowances. The app only ever creates one when the user has none (`ensureStarterData` at sign-up, Start my own list), and the server makes one when a user leaves their only household. Leaving your only household (deleting it, as its last member) and getting a fresh one with a fresh allowance and first month is allowed: it costs every list and recipe, so it isn't worth farming. - **Safety limits**, per user, the same on every plan, in a table (below). Seeded: categorize 60 requests a minute and 500 LLM-bound names a day; step matching 30 a minute and 100 a day; Suggest tags 20 a minute and 50 a day; link import 10 a minute; photo import 5 a minute; recipe imports (link and photo together) 100 a day; AI photos 40 a day. Founding can't reach the last two (its first month allows 100 imports and 40 photos in the whole month); they bound plans with no monthly limit. Null means no limit. A per-minute refusal is 429 `rate_limited` as now; a daily one is a new **429 `daily_limit`** with `resets_at` (the next UTC midnight). In the app: categorize leaves names `pending` for the catch-up, step matching stops for the session, and the import sheet, photo import, Suggest tags and AI photos say "You've reached today's limit. Try again tomorrow." ("Llegaste al límite de hoy. Inténtalo mañana."). Only two live users, both on unlimited: no edge cases for existing assignments, and this month's usage isn't carried over (household counting starts at the migration). Old app builds must keep working until the last task: a request with no household falls back as each task says, and `my_features` keeps answering the old feature keys. Never deploy to hosted Supabase: leave the commands in progress.md.
title: Requests name their household
text: Requests name their household (spec 4.12, the Edge Functions paragraph). Add an optional `householdId: z.string().uuid()` to `RecipeImportRequestSchema`, `RecipePhotoImportRequestSchema`, `SuggestRecipeTagsRequestSchema` and `MatchRecipeStepsRequestSchema` (`src/shared/schemas/`; optional so old builds' requests still parse). `import-recipe` and `import-recipe-photo` pass it to `requireFeature(admin, userId, 'recipe_import', householdId)`; all four pass it into `runAiTask`'s `caller`, so `ai_calls.household_id` is set. `generate-recipe-photo` checks the recipe's household: today it calls `requireFeature` with no household before `reserve` (which counts usage), so add a read-only store lookup of the live recipe's household first (`not_found` as now when it's gone), pass that to `requireFeature`, then reserve; an unentitled call still writes nothing. For the two imports, a household the caller isn't in answers 403 `not_entitled` before any work; for tags and step matching, a household the caller isn't in is ignored (no `household_id` on the row). The app sends it: `src/features/recipes/import.ts` (the household the recipe is saved to, link and photo), `suggest-tags.ts` and `ensure-step-match.ts` (the recipe's `household_id`). Update the CLIs only as needed to keep them running (no household). Deno tests per function: the household reaches `requireFeature` (imports) and the `ai_calls` caller; a non-member import is 403 with nothing written; no household still works. Jest: each call site's request body has the household.
notes: Requests name their household (spec 4.12 Edge Functions paragraph). The four request schemas gained an optional `householdId: z.uuid()` (the repo's Zod v4 idiom, not the deprecated `z.string().uuid()`).

title: Monthly allowance per household
text: Monthly allowance per household (spec 4.12 Monthly limits, Checking; 5 AI usage counters). A migration: `private.household_ai_usage (household_id uuid references households on delete cascade, feature text, day date, used integer not null default 0, primary key (household_id, feature, day))`, RLS on, privileges revoked as the other usage tables, pruned after 40 days by the existing daily job. `check_recipe_import_limit` and `check_recipe_photo_limit` gain `p_household_id` (null, from an old client: the user's oldest household) and both check and count the household's `recipe_import`: the monthly check sums `private.monthly_usage(household, 'recipe_import')` (from `household_ai_usage`) against `private.monthly_limit('recipe_import', household)`, under a per-household advisory lock, after the safety limits, then counts the request on the user's own table (for the safety limits) and on `household_ai_usage`. `reserve_recipe_photo_ai` does the same for `recipe_photo_ai` with the recipe's household, keeping its `blocked` answer first, before any limit check. Drop the transition `monthly_limit(user, feature, household)` wrapper. Each function's store passes the household. No backfill: the month's household counts start at zero. pgTAP (`48_plan_limits.test.sql` and the functions' own tests): two members of one household share one allowance; link and photo imports share it; a member's use in household A doesn't count in household B; a refused request counts nothing; a null household counts against the oldest. Deno tests for the stores' new argument.
notes: Monthly allowance per household (spec 4.12 Monthly limits, Checking; 5): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261201120000_household_ai_usage.sql`: `private.household_ai_usage` (key household, feature, day; `feature` checked to the two plan keys; `used >= 0`; cascade on household delete; RLS on; revoked from public/anon/authenticated) and a `household-ai-usage-retention` cron job (`51 3 * * *`, 40 days; each usage table has its own job, so "the existing daily job" became one more in the same style). New private helpers: `oldest_household(user)` (created_at, then id), `check_household_monthly_limit(user, household, feature)` ('monthly_limit' for a household the user isn't in or none; else takes a per-household-per-feature advisory lock and compares `monthly_usage` with `monthly_limit(feature, household)`) and `count_household_ai_usage`. `private.monthly_usage` is now `(household, feature)` from `household_ai_usage` (dropped and recreated: same argument types). `check_recipe_import_limit` and `check_recipe_photo_limit` were dropped and recreated as `(p_user_id, p_household_id default null)` (null: the oldest household), checking safety limits, then the month, then counting on the user's table and the household's; `reserve_recipe_photo_ai` does the same for `recipe_photo_ai` with the recipe's household, `blocked` still first. The `monthly_limit(user, feature, household)` wrapper is dropped. Its two remaining readers, `admin_user_detail` (usage `used`/`limit`) and `admin_ai_usage` (`top_users` limit), now read the user's oldest household until the portal task rewrites them. Stores: `checkLimit(householdId?)` sends `p_household_id` (null when absent), and both handlers pass `request.householdId`. Photo import's server message for `monthly_limit` is now "This month's recipe imports are used up" (the app's strings are the next task). `docs/admin.md`'s usage snippet uses the household signatures.

title: The app's features per household
text: The app's features per household (spec 4.12 In the app). `src/features/plans/`: the store holds `{ households: Record<id, Feature[]> }` from `my_household_features()` (cached in device settings with the user id as now; an old cached shape is ignored), `Feature` being `recipe_import` and `recipe_photo_ai`; `hasFeature(feature, householdId)` and `useFeature(feature, householdId)`, a household the answer doesn't have yet assuming the default plan (founding: both), as before the first answer; `useAnyHouseholdFeature(feature)`. Reload on sign-in, foreground, reconnect and when memberships change (after a join, leave, delete or a new household). `lostFeature(feature, householdId)` drops it for that household. Remove the gates on what's now for everyone: categorize always sends (`categories.ts`, the catch-up, the list and item screens), **Suggest tags** always shows (`recipe/[id]/tags.tsx`, `index.tsx`), and `ensure-step-match.ts` always matches. Call sites that stay gated: the recipe screens' AI photo (`recipe/[id]/photo.tsx`, `index.tsx`) use the recipe's household; the Recipes tab's Import from link buttons, the list menu's Add recipe from link… and the Add recipe sheet's link and From photo… use `useAnyHouseholdFeature('recipe_import')`. In the import sheet (`import-sheet.ts`, `src/app/add-recipe.tsx`), a Save to household whose plan lacks `recipe_import` disables the button with "Recipe import isn't included in {{household}}'s plan." under it, for link and photo alike (`en.ts` and `es.ts`: "La importación de recetas no está incluida en el plan de {{household}}."). Photo import's `limit_reached` says "You've used this month's recipe imports…" like link import, since they share the allowance; delete the "this month's photo imports" and "this month's tag suggestions" strings if nothing uses them. Jest (`src/features/plans/__tests__/`, `categories/__tests__/plans.test.ts`, the screen tests that mock features): per-household answers, the default for an unknown household, caching and the ignored old shape, `lostFeature` for one household, reload on a membership change; the import sheet disabled for one household and enabled after switching; Suggest tags and step matching with no feature at all; categorize sends for a user on none.
notes: The app's features per household (spec 4.12 In the app): DONE, checked off. App only, no `supabase/` changes. `src/features/plans/features.ts` holds `my_household_features()`'s answer (`{ [household]: Feature[] }`, null before the first), `Feature` = `recipe_import` | `recipe_photo_ai`; `hasFeature(feature, householdId)` / `useFeature(feature, householdId)` (a household missing from the answer, or no answer yet, gets founding's two), `hasAnyHouseholdFeature` / `useAnyHouseholdFeature` (the device's households, live, plus the answer's; none known: the default), `parseHouseholdFeatures` (null for any other shape, so the old cached list is ignored). `load.ts` calls `my_household_features`, caches `{ userId, households }`, `lostFeature(feature, householdId)` drops it for that household only (no household: only reloads), and `membershipsRead(households)` reloads when a full pull's household list differs from the answer's; `app-data.tsx` wires it to `onMemberships` (kept out of `load.ts`, since importing `sync/pull` pulls in auth/Google sign-in). Ungated: categorize always sends (`startCategorizeOnGain` and `isNotEntitled` removed; a pending name has no default unit; an old server's `not_entitled` just leaves names pending), the `sorts` parameter is gone from `groupItems`/`effectiveCategoryId` and the list and item screens; Suggest tags always shows (`tags.tsx`, `recipe/[id]/index.tsx`), its `limit-reached` failure is gone (an old server's `limit_reached` is `failed`); step matching always runs (its `not_entitled` still stops the session, as `daily_limit` does). Gated by household: the AI photo row (`photo.tsx`, the recipe's household) and generation's `not_entitled`/`ai_photos_blocked` drop it for the recipe's household; an import's `not_entitled` drops `recipe_import` for the household it saved to (link and photo alike). The Recipes tab's Import from link and the Add recipe sheet's link handling and From photo… use `useAnyHouseholdFeature('recipe_import')`. The import sheet (`import-recipe.tsx`): a Save to household without `recipe_import` disables Save (and Return) with "Recipe import isn't included in {{household}}'s plan." under it (`householdImportNote` in `import-sheet.ts`; `recipes.import.householdNotEntitled` in en/es). `importLimitMessage` lost its `from`: photo imports say "this month's recipe imports"; deleted `photoLimitReached` and `recipes.tags.errors.limitReached` (en, es). There is no list-menu "Add recipe from link…" any more, so nothing to change there.
manualChecks: App: photo-size toggle with large tiles: on a device, on the Recipes tab in light and dark, the photo-size toggle sits last in the header row after the sort pill, the selected segment white with a green glyph; both segments are easy to hit. Tap Large photos: recipes become two tiles per row inside the household card (and inside each meal card in By meal), photos crop well at 4:3 (and the small 48 pt photos still crop well in rows), recipes without a photo show their tinted tile with the fork and knife, names wrap to two lines, the "On <list>" badge sits over the photo's top-right corner, a just-imported recipe's tile gets a green outline. Tapping a tile opens the recipe, long-press shows the menu with Delete; tiles don't swipe. Relaunch: Large photos is still chosen. At the largest accessibility text sizes the grid is one column and the header pills wrap instead of clipping. VoiceOver reads the toggle as "Photo size" with each segment's selected state.

Seeded: categorize 60 requests a minute and 500 LLM-bound names a day; step matching 30 a minute and 100 a day; Suggest tags 20 a minute and 50 a day; link import 10 a minute; photo import 5 a minute; recipe imports (link and photo together) 100 a day; AI photos 40 a day. Founding can't reach the last two (its first month allows 100 imports and 40 photos in the whole month); they bound plans with no monthly limit. Null means no limit. A per-minute refusal is 429 `rate_limited` as now; a daily one is a new **429 `daily_limit`** with `resets_at` (the next UTC midnight). In the app: categorize leaves names `pending` for the catch-up, step matching stops for the session, and the import sheet, photo import, Suggest tags and AI photos say "You've reached today's limit. Try again tomorrow." ("Llegaste al límite de hoy. Inténtalo mañana."). Only two live users, both on unlimited: no edge cases for existing assignments, and this month's usage isn't carried over (household counting starts at the migration). Old app builds must keep working until the last task: a request with no household falls back as each task says, and `my_features` keeps answering the old feature keys. Never deploy to hosted Supabase: leave the commands in progress.md.

goal: Goal: a plan belongs to a household, not a user, and covers only the two AI features that cost real money: **recipe import** (link and photo, one allowance; the tags and step match an import makes are part of it) and **AI photos**. Everyone in a household gets its plan and shares its monthly allowance, so inviting people doesn't multiply it. Everything else the AI does is for everyone on every plan with no monthly limit: **categorize** (it fills the global catalog, so it helps everyone, and nobody gains from overusing it), **step matching** for recipes typed or edited by hand, and **Suggest tags**. Those keep per-user per-minute limits and gain per-user daily ceilings, which stop a scripted account rather than a person. Every number (the plans' monthly limits and the per-minute and daily ceilings) is a table row an admin edits in the portal, never a constant in code. Decisions behind it, for the spec task to write down: - **Feature keys** become two: `recipe_import` (link import and photo import alike; `recipe_import_photo` folds into it) and `recipe_photo_ai`. `categorize`, `step_ingredients` and `recipe_tags` stop being plan features. The import rule (an import needs `categorize`, `plan_features_import_needs_categorize`) goes away with them. - **Plans**, renamed so the names say what they are: **founding** ("Founding", replacing plus: `recipe_import` 50 a month, `recipe_photo_ai` 20 a month; the default until paid plans launch), **unlimited** (both, no monthly limit), **free** ("Free", replacing none: neither, though categorize, step matching and Suggest tags still work). **basic** is deleted (it had only categorize and step matching, which everyone now has); a household on it moves to free. The ids change too (they're referenced by `household_plans` and the audit log, so this is the last cheap moment): plus becomes `founding` and none becomes `free`; old audit rows keep the old ids as written. A household's first 30 days (`households.created_at`) get twice its plan's monthly limits, as now. - **Every household has an explicit plan.** A household's plan is its `household_plans` row and nothing else; there's no "unassigned, so the default". Creating a household (`create_household`, `private.create_personal_household`) writes its row with the plan that is the default at that moment, and the migration gives every existing household one. "Default" only means the plan new households start on: changing it never moves an existing household. A household with no row (which shouldn't exist) has no features. In the portal a household's plan can be changed to another plan but not cleared. - **Founding households** (every household made before paid plans launch) stay on founding, free of charge, for good, through their explicit rows. Until paid plans launch, new features may be added to founding; after that, founding is frozen: a new feature goes into a new plan, never into founding, so founders get only what founding had at launch. Changing founding's limits is allowed and applies to founders. `docs/admin.md` gets a "Launching paid plans" section: create the paid plan (its own name) and make it the default (new households only); existing households keep founding; never add a feature to founding. - **One household per new user.** `create_household` refuses (`already in a household`, `P0001`) when the caller is already a member of any household, so a user can't make extra households to multiply allowances. The app only ever creates one when the user has none (`ensureStarterData` at sign-up, Start my own list), and the server makes one when a user leaves their only household. Leaving your only household (deleting it, as its last member) and getting a fresh one with a fresh allowance and first month is allowed: it costs every list and recipe, so it isn't worth farming. - **Safety limits**, per user, the same on every plan, in a table (below). Try again tomorrow." ("Llegaste al límite de hoy. Inténtalo mañana."). text: Drop per-user plans and the old keys. section: A user's activity log in the portal
goal: Goal: an admin opening a user in the portal sees everything that user did, newest first, and can filter it: every change of theirs that reached the server (lists and items, recipes, the meal plan, aisles, staples, settings, household and invite actions, devices), their AI requests, and what admins did to their account. Only server writes: nothing the app does without writing (opening a screen, searching, viewing a recipe) is logged, and an offline edit shows when it syncs. Each entry is a named action ("item.checked", "plan.added") with the data that action needs to be read and filtered: ids, the names of what it touched as they were then, and small values (a day and meal, a quantity and unit, a role, on/off), never free text the user wrote (notes, recipe text, steps). Kept 90 days; deleting the account deletes its entries. The spec isn't updated yet: the first task does it. Today nothing records who changed a row after it was made (only `recipes.added_by`, `list_item_contributions.added_by`, `meal_plan_entries.added_by`, `ai_calls.user_id` and `admin.admin_actions` say who), so this is new. Why triggers: every write reaches a table, whichever path it took (`apply_mutations`, the household functions, direct writes to `user_settings` and `user_category_order`, the push token functions), so a trigger can't be missed by a path added later. Logging inside `apply_mutations` would miss the other paths and see no more than the trigger does (a table, a row, its fields). The trigger only sees rows, not what the user meant, so it translates each row change into a named action, below; one gesture that writes many rows (a recipe with 20 ingredients) logs many rows that share a `txid`, and the portal folds them. The catalog (names are snapshots, so a later rename doesn't change old entries; every `data` has the household's name as `household` when there is one): - `lists`: `list.created`, `list.renamed`, `list.archived`, `list.unarchived`, `list.deleted`, `list.restored` (`{ list }`, the name; renamed also `from`), `list.edited` (`{ list, fields }` for emoji, colour), `list.reordered` (position only; `{ list }`); `item.added` (from the contribution insert: `{ list, list_id, item, item_id, source, quantity, unit, recipe, recipe_id }`, the last two when `source` is `recipe`), `item.add_undone` (a contribution's `deleted_at` set), `item.checked`, `item.unchecked`, `item.deleted`, `item.restored` (`{ list, item }`), `item.moved` (`list_id` changed: `{ item, from, to }`), `item.renamed` (`{ item, from }`), `item.edited` (`{ list, item, fields }`: note, quantity on a contribution), `item.photo_added`, `item.photo_removed`, `item.merged` (`merged_into` set: `{ list, item, into }`). A `list_items` insert logs nothing when its first contribution comes in the same transaction (check that every path does that; if one doesn't, it logs `item.added` from the item). - `recipes`: `recipe.created` (`{ recipe, source }`, `source` the `source_url`'s host, `photo` or `manual`), `recipe.renamed` (`{ recipe, from }`), `recipe.edited` (`{ recipe, fields }`, field names only, for notes, servings, times, steps and the rest), `recipe.tagged` (`tags` changed: `{ recipe }`), `recipe.photo_added`, `recipe.photo_removed`, `recipe.deleted`, `recipe.restored` (`{ recipe }`); `ingredient.added`, `ingredient.removed`, `ingredient.edited`, `ingredient.reordered` (`{ recipe, recipe_id, ingredient, fields }`). - `plan`: `plan.added` (`{ date, meal, kind, recipe, recipe_id }` or `{ date, meal, kind }` for leftovers, eating out and notes; a note's text isn't kept), `plan.removed`, `plan.restored` (the same), `plan.moved` (`plan_date` or `meal` changed: `{ from: { date, meal }, to: { date, meal }, recipe }`), `plan.reordered` (position only; `{ date, meal, recipe }`). - `aisles`: `aisle.created`, `aisle.renamed` (`{ aisle, from }`), `aisle.deleted`; `aisle.assigned` (an override: `{ ingredient, aisle }`, aisle null for Reset to default); `staple.added`, `staple.removed` (`{ ingredient }`). - `household` (one row per function call, from the function's name; the rows it writes log nothing more): `household.created`, `household.renamed` (`{ household, from }`), `household.deleted`, `household.left`, `household.combine_languages` (`{ on }`), `invite.created` (`{ invite_id }`, never the invited email: someone who never signs up has no account to delete it with), `invite.revoked`, `invite.accepted`, `invite.declined`, `member.removed`, `member.role_changed` (`{ member, member_id, role }`, the member's display name). - `settings`: `settings.default_list` (`{ list }`), `settings.aisle_order` (one row per transaction, however many aisles moved), `settings.notifications` (`{ fields }`). - `devices`: `device.registered`, `device.unregistered` (`{ platform }`).
title: Spec
text: Spec. Write the activity log into `docs/spec.md` before any code, as the rest of this section describes, and keep it in step if a later task changes a detail. 5: a new server-only table `private.user_activity` (`id bigint generated always as identity primary key`, `user_id uuid not null` (no foreign key, like `admin.admin_actions`; `delete_account` deletes the rows itself), `household_id uuid` (null for per-user rows), `created_at timestamptz not null default now()`, `txid bigint not null default txid_current()`, `area text not null` (`lists`, `recipes`, `plan`, `aisles`, `household`, `settings`, `devices`: what the portal filters on), `action text not null` (the catalog below), `entity_id text` (the row's id or key), `data jsonb not null default '{}'`), indexed on (`user_id`, `created_at desc`), (`user_id`, `area`, `created_at desc`) and `created_at`; RLS on, no policies, privileges revoked from every client role; the server-only tables paragraph says it has a user id too. 4.12: a new **User activity** bullet with the action catalog as a table (area, action, when it's logged, its `data`), the function and the portal card. 6.5 Privacy: a new paragraph: the log keeps what each user did, when, and the names of what it touched (still there after the thing itself is deleted), never notes, recipe text or an invited person's email; service role only (admins read it, and opening a user's activity is audited); 90 days; deleted with the account, which is also scrubbed from other users' entries. 4.8: `delete_account` and `admin.delete_user` delete the user's rows and scrub them from other users' entries (the Logging task). `docs/alpha-testing.md`: extend the privacy policy line: actions that reach the server (list, recipe, plan, household and settings changes) are logged with the account and the names of what they touched, kept 90 days, deleted with the account, and admins can read them; and the App Store privacy label must declare Product Interaction, linked to the user. 7.3: `apply_mutations` writes are logged by the table triggers; it sets nothing itself.
notes: Rewrote `searchRecentItems` in `src/features/lists/items.ts` to read the household's `ingredient_usage` rows (hidden rows skipped) pre-filtered in SQL by the existing `p%` / `% p%` LIKE patterns on both `display_name` and `ingredient_name`, ordered by `rankHistory` and cut to `limit` after ranking; it takes an optional `now` for tests and returns `{ key, displayName }` as before. `items.test.ts` had no existing `searchRecentItems` tests to update (the one existing suggestion test, in `categories.test.ts`, passes unchanged), so I added a `searchRecentItems (spec 4.2)` block: key and latest display name; 5 uses 10 days ago outrank 1 use yesterday; a deleted list item stays in history; an undone add leaves nothing; word-start but not mid-word matches; key-only match (`zaatar` for `za'atar`); prefix beats word match; hidden rows and other households excluded; limit applied after ranking; case and whitespace; empty and wildcard-only queries; `%`/`_` stripped rather than treated as wildcards. No existing tests changed.

Docs for ingredient history: `docs/spec.md` §4.2 now describes household history (what counts as a use, history outlives items, one-time backfill), frecency ranking and tiebreaks, the history-first rule (2+ history matches shows history only, else catalog fills in), and "Remove from suggestions"; §5 adds an `ingredient_usage` table as household data synced in M5 with `use_count` merged as a counter (other fields last-writer-wins), plus a note that Siri adds go through `siri-add` and aren't counted until M5 sync. Added `// TODO(M5): sync` above the table in `src/db/schema.ts`. No code tests (docs only); jest, lint and typecheck pass.

Households docs. `docs/spec.md` §10 now has a "Landed early" note under M5. It lists what was pulled forward: `households` and `household_members` (with RLS), `create_household` and `get_household_members`. It also says the app registers its local household via `registerHouseholds` instead of sign-up creating one on the server, which M5 revisits. A matching note under M7 covers the read-only Households screen: invites, rename, leave, remove and roles are still M7, and `household_invites` doesn't exist yet. `README.md` "Looking at the data" now explains how to add a test member. The second user signs in once so they have a profile, then an `insert ... select` into `household_members` matches both users by email and sets position to their max + 1; the section also shows how to remove them again. I also updated the README's out-of-date sentence saying Supabase only handles sign-in and profiles. No code tests (docs only). jest (276), lint and typecheck pass. **The README SQL wasn't run** because psql needs approval in this session, so check it once in Studio.

Quantities docs. `docs/spec.md` §4.2 gains a "Usual unit" bullet. It covers `ingredient_unit_usage`: each add or recipe ingredient with a quantity counts one use of its unit, and count when it has no unit. Undo takes the use back, and an add with no quantity counts nothing. The most-used unit wins; ties go to the most recent, then alphabetical. Existing data is backfilled once. §4.2 also gains a "Changing an amount" bullet for the edit sheet's − / + stepper and unit button, which save immediately. Steps are 1 / 0.5 / 0.25 / 100 depending on the unit, results are rounded to the step, and − stops at one step. An item with no amount steps from one of its usual unit. The unit picker keeps the number without converting. Drag to reorder in As added moves rows live (2026-10-16, spec 4.6): the cause was each row's `onLayout` doing `boxes.set({ ...boxes.get(), [id]: box })` on the JS thread. In Reanimated 4.5 a JS-thread `set` is only scheduled onto the UI thread while `get` reads the UI value now, so rows laying out together overwrote one another and only the last row's box survived. The rest counted as zero height, so nothing made room and the drop slots were wrong. Fix: `boxes.modify(all => withBox(all, id, box))`, which runs in order on the UI thread. Also pulled the drag reaction's math into a pure `dragTo(rows, from, translation, scrolled)` in `row-drag.ts`, placed below `clampDrag` because the worklets plugin turns worklet functions into consts, which aren't hoisted. Tests: `row-drag.test.ts` adds `dragTo` (down and up past several rows including a taller one, across an auto-scroll both ways, clamped at the ends, no boxes) and `withBox`. `reorderable-rows.test.tsx`'s Reanimated mock now defers JS-thread `set`/`modify` until the UI thread runs, as on device (an existing test file's mock changed, no assertions weakened), and adds two tests that the other rows make room live, down and up. The check is written inline with cases, no function, and requires exactly provider 'pexels', author 1–200 chars, and authorUrl/pageUrl that are https:// and ≤ 2048 chars, only when photo_path is set. apply_mutations needed no change. Push and pull are generic, so no mapping code changed. `RecipePhotoFields` now has `photoCredit`, plus a new `RecipePhotoSourceFields` where the credit is optional, so tiles that show no credit don't pass one. `useRecipePhoto` returns `credit`, which is the own photo's credit, else null. pagePhoto and photoAfterRemove clear the credit. changedFields sends `photoCredit` whenever `photoPath` changes, even when the credit is null both times, and also when only the credit differs. Push tokens and notification settings (2026-10-17, spec 4.13, 5). New migration supabase/migrations/20261103120000_push_notifications.sql. public.push_tokens (token pk, user_id cascade + index, platform ios|android, created_at/updated_at with the set_updated_at trigger) has RLS on and no client grants. register_push_token(p_token, p_platform) and unregister_push_token(p_token) are security definer, granted to authenticated only, and raise `not signed in` (42501) without a user. register checks the shape `^(Exponent|Expo)PushToken\[[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\]$` and ≤ 200 chars (`invalid token`, 22023) and the platform (`invalid platform`), then upserts on token: another user's token moves to the caller and updated_at is bumped. unregister deletes only the caller's row and is a no-op otherwise. public.notification_settings (user_id pk cascade, items_added/shopping default true, quiet_hours_start/end, time_zone default 'UTC') checks the quiet hours are both null or both set and different, has a trigger (private.check_notification_time_zone) raising `invalid time zone` (22023) for a name not in pg_timezone_names, and select/insert/update own-row policies (no delete). private.push_recipients(household, actor, kind, at) returns (user_id, token, platform), one row per device, for current members other than the actor, with the kind on (`items_added` | `shopping`, else `invalid kind`) and outside quiet hours [start, end) in their own time zone (start > end wraps midnight); a missing settings row is the defaults. Note for the worker task: `private` isn't exposed by PostgREST (config.toml schemas = public, graphql_public), so supabase-js `.rpc` can't reach push_recipients as is; the worker needs a direct Postgres connection or a public service_role-only wrapper. section: A user's activity log in the portal
goal: Goal: an admin opening a user in the portal sees everything that user did, newest first, and can filter it: every change of theirs that reached the server (lists and items, recipes, the meal plan, aisles, staples, settings, household and invite actions, devices), their AI requests, and what admins did to their account. Only server writes: nothing the app does without writing (opening a screen, searching, viewing a recipe) is logged, and an offline edit shows when it syncs. Each entry is a named action ("item.checked", "plan.added") with the data that action needs to be read and filtered: ids, the names of what it touched as they were then, and small values (a day and meal, a quantity and unit, a role, on/off), never free text the user wrote (notes, recipe text, steps). Kept 90 days; deleting the account deletes its entries. The spec isn't updated yet: the first task does it. Today nothing records who changed a row after it was made (only `recipes.added_by`, `list_item_contributions.added_by`, `meal_plan_entries.added_by`, `ai_calls.user_id` and `admin.admin_actions` say who), so this is new. Why triggers: every write reaches a table, whichever path it took (`apply_mutations`, the household functions, direct writes to `user_settings` and `user_category_order`, the push token functions), so a trigger can't be missed by a path added later. Logging inside `apply_mutations` would miss the other paths and see no more than the trigger does (a table, a row, its fields). The trigger only sees rows, not what the user meant, so it translates each row change into a named action, below; one gesture that writes many rows (a recipe with 20 ingredients) logs many rows that share a `txid`, and the portal folds them. The catalog (names are snapshots, so a later rename doesn't change old entries; every `data` has the household's name as `household` when there is one): - `lists`: `list.created`, `list.renamed`, `list.archived`, `list.unarchived`, `list.deleted`, `list.restored` (`{ list }`, the name; renamed also `from`), `list.edited` (`{ list, fields }` for emoji, colour), `list.reordered` (position only; `{ list }`); `item.added` (from the contribution insert: `{ list, list_id, item, item_id, source, quantity, unit, recipe, recipe_id }`, the last two when `source` is `recipe`), `item.add_undone` (a contribution's `deleted_at` set), `item.checked`, `item.unchecked`, `item.deleted`, `item.restored` (`{ list, item }`), `item.moved` (`list_id` changed: `{ item, from, to }`), `item.renamed` (`{ item, from }`), `item.edited` (`{ list, item, fields }`: note, quantity on a contribution), `item.photo_added`, `item.photo_removed`, `item.merged` (`merged_into` set: `{ list, item, into }`). A `list_items` insert logs nothing when its first contribution comes in the same transaction (check that every path does that; if one doesn't, it logs `item.added` from the item). - `recipes`: `recipe.created` (`{ recipe, source }`, `source` the `source_url`'s host, `photo` or `manual`), `recipe.renamed` (`{ recipe, from }`), `recipe.edited` (`{ recipe, fields }`, field names only, for notes, servings, times, steps and the rest), `recipe.tagged` (`tags` changed: `{ recipe }`), `recipe.photo_added`, `recipe.photo_removed`, `recipe.deleted`, `recipe.restored` (`{ recipe }`); `ingredient.added`, `ingredient.removed`, `ingredient.edited`, `ingredient.reordered` (`{ recipe, recipe_id, ingredient, fields }`). - `plan`: `plan.added` (`{ date, meal, kind, recipe, recipe_id }` or `{ date, meal, kind }` for leftovers, eating out and notes; a note's text isn't kept), `plan.removed`, `plan.restored` (the same), `plan.moved` (`plan_date` or `meal` changed: `{ from: { date, meal }, to: { date, meal }, recipe }`), `plan.reordered` (position only; `{ date, meal, recipe }`). - `aisles`: `aisle.created`, `aisle.renamed` (`{ aisle, from }`), `aisle.deleted`; `aisle.assigned` (an override: `{ ingredient, aisle }`, aisle null for Reset to default); `staple.added`, `staple.removed` (`{ ingredient }`). - `household` (one row per function call, from the function's name; the rows it writes log nothing more): `household.created`, `household.renamed` (`{ household, from }`), `household.deleted`, `household.left`, `household.combine_languages` (`{ on }`), `invite.created` (`{ invite_id }`, never the invited email: someone who never signs up has no account to delete it with), `invite.revoked`, `invite.accepted`, `invite.declined`, `member.removed`, `member.role_changed` (`{ member, member_id, role }`, the member's display name). - `settings`: `settings.default_list` (`{ list }`), `settings.aisle_order` (one row per transaction, however many aisles moved), `settings.notifications` (`{ fields }`). - `devices`: `device.registered`, `device.unregistered` (`{ platform }`).
title: Logging writes
text: Logging writes (spec 5, 4.12, 6.5). A migration: the table, and trigger functions in `private` (`security definer`, `search_path = ''`, execute revoked from every client role), one per table (`private.activity_list_items(old, new)` and so on) returning the area, action, entity id and `data` per the catalog, or nothing, and one shared `private.log_user_activity()` trigger, after insert, update or delete for each row, that calls the table's function and inserts the row. It does nothing when `auth.uid()` is null (pg_cron, Edge Functions on the service role, the dashboard), and logs nothing for an update whose only changed columns are `updated_at`, `field_clock` or `created_at`. Names in `data` are read from the row or its parent (a list item's list, a contribution's item and list, an ingredient's recipe, a plan entry's recipe); keep those lookups to primary keys. The household functions set a transaction-local `app.activity_action` (`set_config('app.activity_action', ..., true)`) with their action and `data`; while it's set, the trigger logs that one row on the first write and nothing for the rest. `settings.aisle_order` logs once per transaction the same way. Like the `household_events` triggers, logging never fails the write: an error raises a warning. Attach it to `lists`, `list_items`, `list_item_contributions`, `recipes`, `recipe_ingredients`, `meal_plan_entries`, `categories` (rows with a `household_id`), `household_category_overrides`, `household_staples`, `user_settings`, `user_category_order`, `notification_settings`, `households`, `household_members`, `household_invites` and `push_tokens`; not `ingredient_usage` / `ingredient_unit_usage` (counters). Check that `auth.uid()` is the caller inside `apply_mutations` and the household functions. Retention: a daily pg_cron job `user-activity-retention` deletes rows older than 90 days. `delete_account` / `private.delete_user_core` delete the user's rows last, so the account's own deletes leave none, and scrub the user from other users' entries: in `member.removed` and `member.role_changed` rows whose `data.member_id` is the user, remove `member` and `member_id` from `data` (the portal then says "a member"). pgTAP (a new `5x_user_activity.test.sql`): through `apply_mutations`, one test per catalog action that a sync makes (each with its `data`), an update touching only ignored columns logging nothing, a recipe with three ingredients giving one `recipe.created` and three `ingredient.added` with one `txid`; each household function logging its one action; a write with no `auth.uid()` logging nothing; a client can't read the table; `delete_account` leaving no rows of the user's and scrubbing another member's `member.removed` entry about them; no `invite.created` row holds an email; the retention delete. Time a 200-mutation push before and after and write both in progress.md.

No app, admin or Edge Function code changed. No real AI calls. **Hosted step for the user (not run):** `supabase db push`.

section: A user's activity log in the portal
goal: Goal: an admin opening a user in the portal sees everything that user did, newest first, and can filter it: every change of theirs that reached the server (lists and items, recipes, the meal plan, aisles, staples, settings, household and invite actions, devices), their AI requests, and what admins did to their account. Only server writes: nothing the app does without writing (opening a screen, searching, viewing a recipe) is logged, and an offline edit shows when it syncs. Each entry is a named action ("item.checked", "plan.added") with the data that action needs to be read and filtered: ids, the names of what it touched as they were then, and small values (a day and meal, a quantity and unit, a role, on/off), never free text the user wrote (notes, recipe text, steps). Kept 90 days; deleting the account deletes its entries. The spec isn't updated yet: the first task does it. Today nothing records who changed a row after it was made (only `recipes.added_by`, `list_item_contributions.added_by`, `meal_plan_entries.added_by`, `ai_calls.user_id` and `admin.admin_actions` say who), so this is new. Why triggers: every write reaches a table, whichever path it took (`apply_mutations`, the household functions, direct writes to `user_settings` and `user_category_order`, the push token functions), so a trigger can't be missed by a path added later. Logging inside `apply_mutations` would miss the other paths and see no more than the trigger does (a table, a row, its fields). The trigger only sees rows, not what the user meant, so it translates each row change into a named action, below; one gesture that writes many rows (a recipe with 20 ingredients) logs many rows that share a `txid`, and the portal folds them. The catalog (names are snapshots, so a later rename doesn't change old entries; every `data` has the household's name as `household` when there is one): - `lists`: `list.created`, `list.renamed`, `list.archived`, `list.unarchived`, `list.deleted`, `list.restored` (`{ list }`, the name; renamed also `from`), `list.edited` (`{ list, fields }` for emoji, colour), `list.reordered` (position only; `{ list }`); `item.added` (from the contribution insert: `{ list, list_id, item, item_id, source, quantity, unit, recipe, recipe_id }`, the last two when `source` is `recipe`), `item.add_undone` (a contribution's `deleted_at` set), `item.checked`, `item.unchecked`, `item.deleted`, `item.restored` (`{ list, item }`), `item.moved` (`list_id` changed: `{ item, from, to }`), `item.renamed` (`{ item, from }`), `item.edited` (`{ list, item, fields }`: note, quantity on a contribution), `item.photo_added`, `item.photo_removed`, `item.merged` (`merged_into` set: `{ list, item, into }`). A `list_items` insert logs nothing when its first contribution comes in the same transaction (check that every path does that; if one doesn't, it logs `item.added` from the item). - `recipes`: `recipe.created` (`{ recipe, source }`, `source` the `source_url`'s host, `photo` or `manual`), `recipe.renamed` (`{ recipe, from }`), `recipe.edited` (`{ recipe, fields }`, field names only, for notes, servings, times, steps and the rest), `recipe.tagged` (`tags` changed: `{ recipe }`), `recipe.photo_added`, `recipe.photo_removed`, `recipe.deleted`, `recipe.restored` (`{ recipe }`); `ingredient.added`, `ingredient.removed`, `ingredient.edited`, `ingredient.reordered` (`{ recipe, recipe_id, ingredient, fields }`). - `plan`: `plan.added` (`{ date, meal, kind, recipe, recipe_id }` or `{ date, meal, kind }` for leftovers, eating out and notes; a note's text isn't kept), `plan.removed`, `plan.restored` (the same), `plan.moved` (`plan_date` or `meal` changed: `{ from: { date, meal }, to: { date, meal }, recipe }`), `plan.reordered` (position only; `{ date, meal, recipe }`). - `aisles`: `aisle.created`, `aisle.renamed` (`{ aisle, from }`), `aisle.deleted`; `aisle.assigned` (an override: `{ ingredient, aisle }`, aisle null for Reset to default); `staple.added`, `staple.removed` (`{ ingredient }`). - `household` (one row per function call, from the function's name; the rows it writes log nothing more): `household.created`, `household.renamed` (`{ household, from }`), `household.deleted`, `household.left`, `household.combine_languages` (`{ on }`), `invite.created` (`{ invite_id }`, never the invited email: someone who never signs up has no account to delete it with), `invite.revoked`, `invite.accepted`, `invite.declined`, `member.removed`, `member.role_changed` (`{ member, member_id, role }`, the member's display name). - `settings`: `settings.default_list` (`{ list }`), `settings.aisle_order` (one row per transaction, however many aisles moved), `settings.notifications` (`{ fields }`). - `devices`: `device.registered`, `device.unregistered` (`{ platform }`).
title: Reading a user's activity
text: Reading a user's activity (spec 4.12). `admin_user_activity(p_user_id, p_areas text[] default null, p_actions text[] default null, p_household_id default null, p_from timestamptz default null, p_to timestamptz default null, p_before timestamptz default null, p_limit default 100)` (jsonb, `security definer`, admins only as the other `admin_*` functions). Opening a user's activity is audited, as opening an AI call is: a call with no `p_before` (the first page, whatever the filters) writes one `admin.admin_actions` row (`view_user_activity`, the user as `target_user_id`, `details` the filters, no note, `performed_by` the admin's id); later pages write nothing. It returns `{ entries, next_before, counts }`, newest first, at most 200 entries, keyset paged on `p_before` (`next_before` null at the end), every filter combining. It merges three sources, each entry `{ at, source, area, action, entity_id, household_id, household, txid, data }`: `private.user_activity` (`source` `app`); the user's `ai_calls` (`source` `ai`, `area` `ai`, `action` `ai.<task>`, `data` `{ id, status, flag, recipe_id }`, no prompt or output); and `admin.admin_actions` with the user as `target_user_id` (`source` `admin`, `area` `admin`, `action` `admin.<action>`, `data` `{ details, note, performed_by_email }`). `p_areas` takes `ai` and `admin` too. An `invite.created` entry gets `invited_email` from `household_invites` while that invite exists (null once it's gone). `counts` is per area over the same user, households and dates but not `p_areas` or `p_actions`, so the filter chips can show numbers. `admin_user_detail` gains `last_active_at` (the newest `app` or `ai` entry, or null), keeping every field it has (the household plans and the AI photo block). pgTAP: non-admins refused; the first page writes one `view_user_activity` row and a later page none; an invite's email shows while the invite exists and not after; the three sources merge in order; each filter; `counts`; paging returns every row once; an unknown user returns no entries, not an error (a deleted user's admin rows are still listed).
notes: Reading a user's activity (spec 4.12): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261205120000_admin_user_activity.sql`: `private.user_activity_rows(user, household, from, to)` (security definer, no client execute) unions the user's `private.user_activity` (`source` `app`, `household` the snapshot in `data`, else the household's current name), their `ai_calls` (`ai`, `ai.<task>`, `entity_id` the call id, `data` `{ id, status, flag, recipe_id }`) and the `admin.admin_actions` rows targeting them (`admin`, `admin.<action>`, `entity_id` the action id, `data` `{ details, note, performed_by_email }`, the email looked up when `performed_by` is a user id). `public.admin_user_activity(...)` (`require_admin()` first, execute for authenticated only) filters by areas, full action names, household and dates; orders newest first (ties: app, ai, admin, then newer app id first); clamps the limit to 1–200; adds `invited_email` to `invite.created` from `household_invites` (null once the invite is gone); returns `counts` for all nine areas (zeros included) over user, household and dates only; and on a first page (no `p_before`) writes one `view_user_activity` row (`details` `{ areas, actions, household_id, from, to }`, no note, `performed_by` the admin). It writes that row after building the result, so the view isn't in its own page. `admin_user_detail` is re-created unchanged plus `last_active_at` (the later of the newest user_activity entry and the newest AI call). **Judgement calls:** dates are `p_from` inclusive and `p_to` exclusive (the portal task should send the day after the range's end). Keyset paging is on the timestamp alone, so a page never splits one timestamp (one transaction's entries share `now()`): when the limit falls inside a timestamp, the page stops before it. If one timestamp fills the whole page, it comes back whole even past the limit (otherwise those rows would be skipped or paging would stall), so "at most 200" holds except for a single transaction with more entries than the limit. `next_before` is the page's oldest time. An unknown user's first page still writes its audit row. **Tests added:** pgTAP `63_admin_user_activity.test.sql` (50): privileges; non-admin and anon refused, with no audit row written; the three sources merge in order, with the tie order; exact app/ai/admin entry shapes (no prompt); `invited_email` while the invite exists, null for a gone invite and after deleting one, never copied into the log, and no key on other entries; counts (every area, ignoring areas/actions/before, following household and dates); each filter and their combination; paging by 2 returns all 12 once and in order, with page sizes [2,2,2,2,3,1]; a page stopping before a split timestamp; the limit capped; the first page writes one audit row with the filters and a later page none; an unknown user returns no entries; a deleted user's admin rows are listed; `last_active_at` (app newer than AI, AI alone, null with neither). **Existing test changed (behaviour changed by the task):** `50_admin_users` test 28's exact key list for `admin_user_detail` gains `last_active_at`. **Checks:** jest (5396 passed, 2 skipped), lint, tsc; `supabase db reset`, `supabase test db` (63 files, 2066 tests). Note: running `supabase test db` a second time without a reset fails `44_item_photos` 33, `45_recipe_pages` 35–36 and `46_recipe_photo_ai` 28 (apparently leftover state from the previous run). They pass after a reset and don't touch this change. No app or admin code changed. No real AI calls. **Hosted step for the user (not run):** `supabase db push`.

title: The Activity card on the user page
text: The Activity card on the user page (spec 4.12). Portal (`admin/`, follow `admin/AGENTS.md`): the user page (`admin/app/(portal)/users/[id]/page.tsx`) gains an **Activity** card after Households. Filters, kept in the URL's search params so a filtered view can be linked: area chips with counts (All, Lists, Recipes, Plan, Aisles, Household, Settings, Devices, AI, Admin), an action select listing the chosen areas' actions, a household select (the user's households) and a date range. Entries grouped by day (Today, Yesterday, then the date), each with its time, an area icon, and a sentence built in a new `admin/lib/user-activity.ts` (`admin/lib/activity.ts` is the admin Activity page's wording) from the action and `data` ("Checked *Cucumber* on *Groceries*", "Added 2 cups *Flour* to *Groceries* from *Banana bread*", "Planned *Lasagna* for Tue 3 Nov dinner", "Moved *Lasagna* from Tue dinner to Wed dinner", "Edited recipe *Lasagna*: servings, notes", "Invited *a@b.com* to *Home*" ("Invited someone" once the invite is gone), "Removed a member" for a scrubbed entry, "Import recipe failed" linking to the AI call, "Admin changed plan: …" with the note), the household as a muted suffix; entries with the same action in one `txid` fold into one line with a count ("Added 12 ingredients to *Lasagna*"), expandable. An unknown action still shows its name and `data`. **Load older** fetches the next page. The header gains "Last active" from `last_active_at`. Empty state: "Nothing in the last 90 days". The admin Activity page (`/activity`, wording in `admin/lib/activity.ts`) gains the label "Viewed a user's activity" for `view_user_activity`, with the user as its target. Update `admin/lib/types.ts` and `docs/admin.md` (what's logged, what isn't, 90 days, the catalog, that viewing is audited). Portal tests (`yarn --cwd admin test`) for the sentence builder (every catalog action, folding, an unknown action) and the filters' URL round trip; lint and `tsc --noEmit`. In progress.md, list the hosted steps for the user to run (db push), and note that the log starts empty on hosted: nothing before the migration is recorded.
notes: The Activity card on the user page (spec 4.12): DONE, checked off. Portal only, no SQL. New `admin/lib/user-activity.ts`: the nine areas and the catalog's actions with their area and label (`APP_ACTIONS`); AI tasks worded as verbs ("Import recipe"); the action filter's choices for the chosen areas (catalog, `ai.<task>`, the user-targeted `admin.<action>`s, plus the current one when unknown); `entrySentence` for every catalog action from its `data` as the triggers write it (names as emphasised parts; a missing name shows `?`), AI entries ("Import recipe failed", "… refused", "· Not food", linking to `/ai-calls/<id>`), admin entries ("Admin changed plan: founding → unlimited (admin email)" for `set_household_plan`/`set_user_plan`, else "Admin: <label>: <summary>" from `actionSummary`, with the note), and an unknown action as its name plus its `data` as JSON; `householdSuffix` (none for the household area, whose sentences name the household); `foldEntries` (same `txid` and action, one line where the first one was, order kept; entries with no `txid` never fold) and `lineSentence` ("Added 12 ingredients to *Lasagna*"; the list or recipe only when every entry shares it; "from *recipe*" when every item came from one; otherwise the first sentence plus "and N more"); `dayLabel`/`timeText`/`groupByDay` (Today, Yesterday, "Monday, Oct 19, 2026", in the portal's time zone); the filters' URL (`?areas=lists,ai&action=&household=&from=&to=`; parsing drops unknown areas, a household that isn't a uuid, impossible dates and an action outside the chosen areas), `toggleArea`, `areaCounts` and `userActivityArgs` (UTC days, `p_to` the day after To because the function's end is exclusive, limit 100). `lib/user-activity-actions.ts`: the `loadOlderUserActivity` server action (re-parses the filters from the search string; later pages aren't audited). Components: `user-activity-filters.tsx` (chips with counts, action, household, From/To, each `router.replace` into the URL) and `user-activity-list.tsx` (days; lines with time, area icon, sentence and suffix; folds as `<details>`; Load older appends; keyed by the filters so a change resets it). The user page gains the Activity card after Households (in its own Suspense; empty state "Nothing in the last 90 days", or "Nothing matches these filters" with Clear filters when filtered) and "Last active" in the header. `admin/lib/activity.ts`: `view_user_activity` labelled "Viewed a user's activity" (in the filter; its target is the user through the existing target logic), a summary of its filters ("No filters" with none), and `rawSummary` exported. `types.ts`: `last_active_at`, `UserActivityEntry`, `AdminUserActivity`. `docs/admin.md`: new "Follow a user's activity" (what's logged and what isn't, the catalog by area, 90 days, the log starting empty, that viewing is audited, a SQL query). **Judgement calls:** areas are multi-select chips (the spec says "the chosen areas"); dates are UTC days; household-area sentences name the household themselves, so they get no suffix; every AI entry links to its call, not only failed ones. **Tests added:** `admin/lib/user-activity.test.ts` (95): every catalog action's sentence (and a check that the test's list equals `APP_ACTION_KEYS`), adds by hand and without a contribution, recipe sources, plan kinds and long moves, Reset to default, Invited someone (gone invite), scrubbed member entries, the household fallback, missing names, unknown actions, AI and admin sentences, the suffix, folding (12 ingredients, interleaved actions, no txid, unshared context, the recipe source, "and N more"), day labels in UTC and New York, the time, grouping, the URL round trip and its dropping rules, toggling, the function's arguments, the action options and `areaCounts`. `activity.test.ts` gains `view_user_activity` (label, filter, target, summary). **Existing test changed (behaviour changed by the task):** `activity.test.ts` "labels every portal action" gains "Viewed a user's activity". **Checks:** portal tests (325 passed), portal lint, `tsc --noEmit` and `build`; root jest (5396 passed, 2 skipped), lint, tsc. No `supabase/` change, so no db reset or pgTAP run. No real AI calls. Manual check added to manual-checks.md. **Hosted steps for the user (not run):** 1. `supabase db push` (the two activity migrations, `20261204120000_user_activity.sql` and `20261205120000_admin_user_activity.sql`, if not already pushed). 2. Redeploy the portal. **Note:** the log starts empty on hosted. Nothing before the migration is recorded, so a user's card shows only AI calls and admin actions (which come from older tables) until they make changes after the push.
manualChecks: The Activity card on the user page: with local Supabase and `yarn admin`, make some changes in the app as a test user (add a recipe with several ingredients, add it to a list, check items, plan it and move it, invite someone, change a setting), then open that user in the portal. The header shows "Last active"; the Activity card (after Households) lists the changes under Today with times, area icons and the household as a muted suffix; the recipe's ingredients fold into "Added N ingredients to *Recipe*", which expands; the chips show counts and filter (several at once, All clears them), the action select follows the chosen areas, the household select and From/To filter, and the URL keeps them (reload, or paste it in a new tab). Load older appends the next page when there are more than 100 entries. A user with no entries says "Nothing in the last 90 days". Activity (`/activity`) shows a "Viewed a user's activity" row per first page, with the user as the target. Check in light and dark.
