title: Aisle order per household, server
text: Aisle order per household, server (spec 4.3.3, 5, 7.3, 4.12 activity). One migration: drop `user_category_order` and its data, with its realtime publication entry, grants, `private.activity_user_category_order` and its trigger/dispatch entries in `private.log_user_activity`. Create `household_category_order` (key `household_id`, `category_ids jsonb`, `updated_by` set by the server, `field_clock`; members read; written only through `apply_mutations`, `category_ids` as one LWW field, insert or update, no delete) and `user_household_category_order` (key `(user_id, household_id)`, `category_ids jsonb`; RLS select/insert/update/delete only for `user_id = auth.uid()` and a current member of `household_id`; written directly). Both reject with `invalid aisle order` anything but an array of distinct category ids that are system categories or custom ones of the same household. `private.remove_member_from_household` deletes the leaver's personal row. Add both to realtime, and the activity entries `aisles` / `aisle_order.saved` and `settings` / `settings.aisle_order` (`{ household, removed }`). Old clients that still push `user_category_order` must get a permanent rejection, not a retryable error (check how push.ts classifies the failure, and make it permanent on the client too). pgTAP: member vs non-member reads and writes for both tables, validation (duplicates, another household's custom aisle, non-array), LWW by HLC on `category_ids`, leaver's row deleted, activity rows written.
notes: Aisle order per household, server (spec 4.3.3, 5, 7.3, 4.12): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261207120000_household_aisle_order.sql`: `private.log_user_activity()` re-created without the `user_category_order` branch and with branches for the two new tables (otherwise unchanged; the actor is still `auth.uid()`); `private.activity_user_category_order` dropped; the table taken out of `supabase_realtime` and dropped with its data, grants, policy and triggers. `private.check_aisle_order(ids, household)` (security definer, no client execute) raises 22023 `invalid aisle order` for anything but a jsonb array of uuid strings that are distinct (compared as uuids, so case doesn't matter), each a system category or a custom one of that household; an empty array is allowed. A `before insert or update of category_ids, household_id` trigger runs it on both tables. `public.household_category_order` (`household_id` pk, `category_ids`, `updated_by`, `field_clock`, plus `created_at`/`updated_at` with `set_updated_at`, which pull's cursors need; spec 5 says most tables have them): members can select, clients can't write, published to realtime. `private.apply_mutation` gains it: key `household_id`; `category_ids` is the only settable field; a client's `updated_by` is dropped; `updated_by` is set to the caller whenever `category_ids` wins; a new row without `category_ids` is refused with `invalid aisle order`; there's no delete path. `public.user_household_category_order` (`(user_id, household_id)` pk, `category_ids`, timestamps): select/insert/update/delete granted, one RLS policy for all four with `user_id = auth.uid()` and `household_id in my_household_ids()`, published to realtime. `private.remove_member_from_household` deletes the leaver's row, which logs nothing beyond the household function's own entry. Activity: `aisles`/`aisle_order.saved` `{ household }` when the household order is inserted or its `category_ids` changes; `settings`/`settings.aisle_order` `{ household, removed }` for each write of your own order (`removed` true on delete), one entry per row (no once-per-transaction guard: a save is one row now). Old clients: PostgREST answers a request on a dropped table with 404 (`PGRST205`, or `42P01` from a stale schema cache), and `isPermanent` in `push.ts` already counts a 404 as a permanent rejection. title: Aisle order screen editing scopes
text: Aisle order screen editing scopes (spec 4.3.3). The source line (Following household aisle order / Using your own aisle order); the **Household order | My order** segmented control, starting on the user's current source, where choosing a side creates or deletes nothing, with its footnote per side; rows show the chosen side's order (household, or default when none; personal, or the current resolved order as the start of a new one). Drags and VoiceOver Move up/down edit a draft only. **Save household order** / **Save my order** under the rows (off until something moved) writes the whole order; saving the household order never deletes the user's own. **Use household order** (only when the user has their own) deletes it, no confirm. With unsaved moves, switching sides or leaving (Done, swipe down) asks "Discard your changes?" (Discard / Keep editing); a modal's swipe-down needs to be blocked while dirty (check the Expo Router SDK docs for the current way). en and es strings, DESIGN.md tokens. Component tests for each rule. Manual check with two users in one household: A saves a household order, B (following) sees it on a list; B saves their own, A changes the household order again, B's list doesn't change; B taps Use household order and sees A's order.
notes: Aisle order screen editing scopes (spec 4.3.3): `category-order.tsx` has the source line (Following household aisle order / Using your own aisle order), a **Household order | My order** `SegmentedControl` that starts on the side the user follows (read synchronously on mount, since the live queries fill in after the first render) and writes nothing, and its footnote per side. Rows show the chosen side (household order or default; the user's own, or the resolved order as the start of one); drags and VoiceOver moves edit a draft only; **Save household order** / **Save my order** (`PrimaryButton` in a new `footer` slot of `AisleOrderList`; off until the draft differs from the side's order, and without a household id) writes the whole order; **Use household order** (plain `Button`, only with an own order) deletes it without a confirm. Replaced `aisleOrder.intro` with the new en/es strings (`docs/i18n/es-review.csv` not regenerated). Server: share import jobs (plan §4): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261210093000_share_imports.sql`: `public.share_imports` as in spec 5 (`status` defaults to `received`; indexes for due work, leases, per user and retention; the `set_updated_at` trigger; RLS on, no client grants) and the view `my_share_imports` (runs as its owner, filters `user_id = auth.uid()`, leaves out `page`/`extraction`/hash/owner/lease; `select` to `authenticated` only). Service-role functions: `claim_share_import(p_kinds text[] default null)` (kinds `extracting`/`committing`, null for both; returns `setof share_imports`, the row with its page; an expired lease that has already used 8 attempts is failed with `lease_lost`/transient instead of claimed), `reserve_share_import` (answers `check_recipe_import_limit`'s `ok`/`user_limit`/`daily_limit`/`monthly_limit`; the worker maps them to its codes), `save_share_extraction`, `release_share_import` (returns the new status; transient backoff from `private.share_import_backoff(attempts)`, 30 s/2 min/10 min/1 h/6 h plus up to 20 % jitter, unless `p_next_attempt_at` is given; waiting is `rate_limited` only, due the next minute, attempts − 1; permanent keeps `p_resets_at`; `failed` nulls `page`). All of them check the lease through `private.leased_share_import` and raise `lease_lost` (55000): save and reserve need an unexpired lease, release only a matching token. For `authenticated`: `retry_share_import` (failed → received, attempts 0, error cleared, `metered_at` kept; any other status is returned unchanged; P0002 for another user's id) and `share_import_status`. The daily cron `share-imports-retention` (03:53) runs `private.share_imports_retention()`; the extraction purge counts from `coalesce(committed_at, updated_at)`. We'll prepare it in the background." shows. Don't open the app: the row appears within seconds and reaches `done`. **2. Airplane mode, then reconnect:** force-quit the app, turn on airplane mode, share and dismiss as in 1. The sheet says the same; no row appears. Turn airplane mode off (Wi-Fi back on) without opening the app: the background upload goes through and the row reaches `done`. If it hasn't after five minutes, open the app: the reconcile submits it, and it's still imported only once. **3. Locked right after sharing:** share, Save, and press the side button at once. Leave the phone locked: the row reaches `done` and the "ready" push shows on the lock screen. **4. Force-quit before sharing and right after:** force-quit the app, share and save, then open the app and force-quit it again within a second or two. One `share_imports` row for that envelope id, one recipe, the items added once; on the next open there's no stuck pending card on the Recipes tab. **5. Second household phone:** with B's app open on the chosen list, and again with it backgrounded, share from A without opening A's app. B gets the recipe in Recipes and its ingredients on the list through sync, A never having opened the app; B gets the household push ("<A> added <recipe> (<n> items) to <list>", with list pushes on) and no "ready" push. **6. Share a recipe and a non-recipe page: the rows still end `done` / `failed`, and A gets neither push (B's household push for the recipe still comes). Turn it back on afterwards.

title: Shared planner, and the app adopts it
text: Shared planner, and the app adopts it (plan §1, §5 Planning). Add `planListAdds(snapshot, adds, meta, unitKnowledge, ids)` and `planRecipeImport({ extracted, target, existingRecipe, listSnapshot, unitKnowledge, ids, at, userId })` in `src/shared/domain/`, returning neutral `writes` (`{ table, id | key, fields, counters? }`), `preconditions` (`combine` item live and unchecked; `reopen` item with its `checked_at` and live contribution ids; `new` with list and key; `recipeAbsent` / `recipeReuse`) and per-add outcomes, following `applyAdd` and `save()` exactly (usage counters, unit usage, Combine, reopen replacing amounts, the import counting uses once). Switch `addItem`, `addSiriItem`, `addItemsBulk` and the import's `save()` (`src/features/lists/items.ts`, `src/features/recipes/import.ts`) to build the snapshot from SQLite, call the planner and run `writes` through `insertRow` / `updateRows` / `upsertRow`; results, undo, toasts and `pendingNames` behave as before. The golden fixtures from the previous task pass unchanged in Jest, and the planner's own tests (including preconditions) run in Jest and Deno. Every existing list, recipe and import test passes.
notes: Shared planner, and the app adopts it (plan §1, §5 Planning): DONE, checked off. **New, pure, in `src/shared/domain/`:** `list-plan.ts` with `planListAdds(snapshot, adds, meta, unitKnowledge, ids)` and `import-plan.ts` with `planRecipeImport({ extracted, target, existingRecipe, listSnapshot, unitKnowledge, ids, at, userId })`. `writes` are in the outbox's wire shape without the HLC (`{ op: 'insert' | 'update' | 'upsert', table, id | key, fields, counters? }`, Postgres names, ISO dates), so the server can hand them to `apply_mutation`; `op` is an addition to the plan's shape, because the device needs to know insert from update. `preconditions`: `combine` (once per snapshot item), `reopen` (item, `checkedAt` ISO, live contribution ids), `new` (list, the family key when the household combines languages, else the own key), `recipeAbsent` / `recipeReuse`. Per-add outcomes carry the combine total as amounts + usual unit (the device formats `totalAmountText`, which needs i18n). **Deviations from the plan's types, needed to match `applyAdd` exactly:** `UnitKnowledge` is per name `{ unitUsage, defaultUnit }` (not a resolved unit), so the planner updates unit history as the batch goes, as the sequential device code did (the counted-one rule and the toast's usual unit see earlier adds' units); `ListSnapshot` also has `families` (each batch name's family key), and its items carry `displayName`, `checkedBy` and live contributions with amounts. Ids are taken in the device's old order (contribution before item; recipe, then its ingredients, then the adds). **Device:** new `src/sync/apply-writes.ts` (`applyWrites` runs writes through `insertRow` / `updateRows` / `upsertRow`); `items.ts` has `addSnapshot` (built from SQLite, live items filtered to the batch's names and families) and `addResults` (pending names via `ensureLocalIngredient`, toast total), and `addItem`, `addSiriItem`, `addItemsBulk` all go through `planListAdds`; `applyAdd`/`decideAdd` are gone. The import's `save()` builds the snapshot, calls `planRecipeImport` and applies its writes; `createImportedRecipe`/`liveIngredientIds` are replaced by `newRecipeId` (the import id's recipe id unless taken). Local-only steps (touching the new recipe's `updated_at`, pending catalog rows, `applyResults`) stay in the adapter. One small change: a reopen's soft-deleted amounts now get the add's `at` rather than a second `new Date()` a few ms later. **Tests:** new `src/shared/domain/__tests__/list-plan.test.ts` (new item with exact writes and id order, no-quantity and bare-number units, Combine with total, open over checked, reopen with deletes/preconditions/`reopened`, latest checked and a reopen with no amounts, same name twice in a batch, one `combine` precondition for several adds, twins with combine on/off and family folding, counted-one on/off cases and units learned within the batch, null adds, null user, `knownUnit`) and `import-plan.test.ts` (new recipe: fields, tags with `saved`, positions, trimmed notes, step match update, uses counted once, preconditions, summary; reuse; recipe-only; missing snapshot throws; step mismatch; null tags/empty steps/host name), both also in `supabase/functions/_shared/shared-domain.test.ts` (`deno test -A shared-domain.test.ts`: 19 passed, 77 steps). The golden fixtures pass unchanged (run with `CI=1`; no fixture file changed). No existing test changed. **Checks:** jest 205 suites, 5457 passed, 2 skipped; lint, tsc. title: Server: per-list lock and activity actor
text: Server: per-list lock and activity actor (plan §0 items 5 and 7, §5 steps 3 and 6, §6). One migration: `private.apply_mutation` takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('list:' || list_id, 0))` before deciding whether a `list_items` write leaves a second open item for its ingredient or family, so two concurrent writers can't both leave one open; `private.log_user_activity` uses `coalesce(auth.uid(), nullif(current_setting('app.actor_uid', true), '')::uuid)` as the actor. pgTAP: two open items for one key from separate transactions end as one open item (simulate with two sessions or by asserting the lock is taken; say which); a write with `app.actor_uid` set and no JWT logs activity for that user; without either, nothing is logged, as now.
notes: Server: per-list lock and activity actor. Migration `20261208121500_list_lock_activity_actor.sql` redefines `private.apply_mutation` (from `household_aisle_order.sql`) to take `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('list:' || list_id, 0))` on every `list_items` write, before the row's own `for update` read (list lock before item locks, so two batches on one list can't deadlock), with the list from the existing row or the fields; an open item moved to another list also locks the new list before the open-item decision. `private.log_user_activity` logs as `coalesce(auth.uid(), nullif(current_setting('app.actor_uid', true), '')::uuid)`. pgTAP `66_list_lock_activity_actor.test.sql` (15 tests) simulates the two transactions by asserting the lock is taken (pg_locks for this backend): a new item, an update by id and a move lock their lists, a `lists` write doesn't; the second open item for a key, written after the first, merges so one stays open; with `app.actor_uid` and no JWT the write is logged for that user; with neither (unset or empty) nothing is logged; with both, `auth.uid()` wins. **Checks:** db reset + `supabase test db` (66 files pass), jest 205 suites (5459 passed, 2 skipped), lint, tsc. One `supabase test db` run in between failed 44–46 because the shared local DB had 40 committed photo-cleanup rows from outside this worktree; after a fresh reset everything passed. No existing test changed. No real AI calls.

title: Server: device credentials
text: Server: device credentials (plan §2). Migration: `public.device_credentials` (`id`, `user_id` references `auth.users` on delete cascade, `installation_id`, `token_hash bytea unique` (sha256), `scopes text[]` default `{share.ingest}`, `created_at`, `last_used_at`, `expires_at` (90 days), `revoked_at`, `revoked_reason`; a partial unique index on `(user_id, installation_id)` where not revoked; no client grants). Edge Function `register-device-credential` (`withSupabase({ auth: 'user' })`): body `{ installationId }`; revokes the live credential for that user and installation after a 24-hour grace (`expires_at = least(expires_at, now() + 24 h)`), creates a new one from 32 random bytes, and returns `{ token, expiresAt }` once (the token is never stored or logged). RPC `revoke_my_device_credential(p_installation_id)` for the signed-in user. Admin: `admin_revoke_device_credentials(p_user_id, p_note)` (`require_admin()`, audited like the other admin RPCs) and a **Revoke device credentials** button with a required note on the user's page in `admin/` (follow `admin/AGENTS.md`; `yarn --cwd admin lint`, `tsc --noEmit` and `test` pass). A shared Deno helper `verifyDeviceCredential(admin, token, scope)` returns the user id, or null for unknown, revoked, expired or out-of-scope tokens, and updates `last_used_at`. pgTAP for the table, the RPCs and the cascade on account deletion; Deno tests for the function and the helper.
notes: Server: device credentials (plan §2): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261209100000_device_credentials.sql` (timestamped before the share-imports task's, whose `credential_id` references it): `public.device_credentials` as in spec 5 (`id` defaults to `gen_random_uuid()`, `expires_at` to now + 90 days, `revoked_reason` checked to `replaced`/`sign_out`/`admin`), the partial unique index `(user_id, installation_id) where revoked_at is null`, RLS on with no policies, nothing granted to anon/authenticated. Four functions: `register_device_credential(p_user_id, p_installation_id, p_token_hash hex)` (service role only; an advisory lock per user+installation, then the live one gets `expires_at = revoked_at = least(expires_at, now() + 24 h)`, `replaced`, and a new row is inserted; returns its `expires_at`; 22023 `invalid credential` for a bad hash); `use_device_credential(p_token_hash, p_scope)` (service role only; one `update … returning user_id` that sets `last_used_at`, so verifying is one atomic statement); `revoke_my_device_credential(p_installation_id)` (authenticated; `sign_out`, now); `admin_revoke_device_credentials(p_user_id, p_note)` (`require_admin()`, `require_note`, `admin`, now, one `revoke_device_credentials` audit row with `{ revoked }`, returned, also for 0). **Choice:** sign-out and admin revocation also revoke a credential still in its 24 h grace (a lost phone may hold the old token), so "live" there means valid, not `revoked_at is null`. Deno: `_shared/device-credentials.ts` (`newDeviceToken` = 32 random bytes as base64url; `hashDeviceToken` = sha256 of the bytes as hex, null unless exactly 32 bytes of base64url; `verifyDeviceCredential(admin, token, scope)` → user id or null, and throws on a DB error rather than returning null). New function `register-device-credential` (`index.ts` with `withSupabase({ auth: 'user' })`; `request.ts`: POST, 1 KB cap, `{ installationId: uuid }`, `cache-control: no-store`, a 500 logs only the error message; `handler.ts` with the store over the RPC; own `deno.json`/`deno.lock`; no config.toml entry, since it verifies the JWT). Admin portal: a Devices card on the user page with **Revoke device credentials** (`components/revoke-device-credentials.tsx`, like Unblock's dialog, required note; `lib/device-credential-actions.ts`; message from `lib/device-credentials.ts`); Activity label "Revoked device credentials" with summary "2 credentials", and `admin.revoke_device_credentials` in the user activity filter; `AdminRevokeDeviceCredentialsResult` type; a `docs/admin.md` section. **Tests:** pgTAP `67_device_credentials.test.sql` (54: table, RLS, privileges of the table and all four functions; register for 90 days; replace with a 24 h grace and only one live; a near-expiry one never gains time; per installation; bad hash, missing installation, duplicate hash, unknown user; a direct second live insert refused by the index; verify live, grace, out of scope, unknown, expired, revoked, and `last_used_at` set only on verified ones; an added scope; clients can't read the table or call the service functions; sign-out is per user and installation and takes the grace one too; re-register after sign-out; admin: non-admin, blank and null note, revokes live and grace but not expired or signed-out, audit row, 0 still audited; cascade on user deletion). Deno `_shared/device-credentials.test.ts` (8: token encoding incl. base64url characters, hash of known bytes, malformed tokens null without a DB call, RPC args, null, DB error) and `register-device-credential/handler.test.ts` (7: exact RPC args and response, a new token each time never sent to the DB, lower-cased id, 400s, 405/413, 500 without the token in logs, no expiry). Admin vitest: `lib/device-credentials.test.ts` plus cases in `activity.test.ts` and `user-activity.test.ts`. **Existing test changed:** `admin/lib/activity.test.ts`'s exact list of action labels gains "Revoked device credentials", since the task adds that action. **Checks:** db reset + `supabase test db` (67 files PASS); the new Deno tests pass (`deno test --no-run index.ts` type-checks the entry); jest 205 suites (5459 passed, 2 skipped); lint; tsc; `yarn --cwd admin lint`, `tsc --noEmit` and `test` (338 passed; I ran `yarn --cwd admin install` first because this worktree had no admin node_modules). No real AI calls.

title: Server: share import jobs
text: Server: share import jobs (plan §4). Migration: `public.share_imports` with the columns in plan §4 (the receipt columns included), a `my_share_imports` view without `page` and `extraction` that lets a user select only their own rows, and no client writes. Service-role RPCs, each a short transaction: `claim_share_import(p_kinds)` (the oldest due `received` / `extracted` row or one with an expired lease, `for update skip locked`, moved to `extracting` / `committing` with a new `lease_token`, `lease_expires_at = now() + 2 min`, `attempts + 1`); `reserve_share_import(p_id, p_lease)` (`ok` at once if `metered_at` is set, else the `check_recipe_import_limit` logic in the same transaction, setting `metered_at` on `ok`); `save_share_extraction(p_id, p_lease, p_extraction)` (only with a matching, unexpired lease; moves to `extracted`); `release_share_import(p_id, p_lease, p_kind, p_code, p_next_attempt_at, p_resets_at)` (transient: back to its earlier state with backoff of 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 1 h, 6 h plus jitter, permanent after 8 attempts; waiting, for `rate_limited` only: due at the next minute without counting an attempt; permanent: `failed` with the code, `page` nulled); `retry_share_import(p_id)` for the owner (`failed` back to `received`, attempts reset, never re-charged once metered); `share_import_status(p_ids uuid[])` for the owner. A daily pg_cron job nulls `page` on finished rows and on any row older than 24 hours, nulls `extraction` 7 days after `done`, and deletes rows older than a year. pgTAP: the transitions, `skip locked` with two claimers, an expired lease's save refused, reserving twice charges once, retry keeps the id and doesn't re-charge, the view hides other users' rows and the payload, retention.
notes: Spec for share import on the server (docs only, no code, no tests added). `docs/spec.md`: 4.8 (sign-out revokes the device credential), 4.9 (snapshot `userId`; envelope `userId`/`v: 2`; `share/upload/` and `share/upload-state/`; the shared Keychain group; Siri's upload now names the device credential instead of the spike marker), 4.10 (extension background upload and "Saved. We'll prepare it in the background."; the server imports; the app reconciles instead of draining; failures and Try again from server state on the sharer's devices only; `daily_limit`/`limit_reached` fail with their reason; dead/archived list → default list, no lists → recipe-only with "Saved *Lemon pasta*. Its list was gone, so nothing was added."; a sharer who left fails permanently, per plan §10, replacing the old "household of the default list" fallback for shares; in-app imports stay on the device; imports card rewritten over envelopes + `my_share_imports`; no share toast), 4.12 (`share-import-worker` checks `recipe_import`; `share_ingest` safety row, 30/min per credential; activity actor `coalesce(auth.uid(), app.actor_uid)` and a `recipe.imported_from_share` catalog row; **Device credentials** bullet with audited `admin_revoke_device_credentials` and the user-page button), 4.13 (the two sharer pushes, `/recipe/<id>` and `/recipes` urls, **Recipe imports** switch; household "added" push now at server commit), 5 (`device_credentials`, `share_imports` (plus `title` and a `list_gone` receipt column, not in the plan), `my_share_imports`, `notification_settings.recipe_imports`, RLS and RPC access, retention job), new 6.12 (the three functions, jobs and states, errors, metering, the commit, privacy, rollout), 7.2 (the server as a writer through `private.apply_mutation`, `srv` HLCs, no pull change), 7.3 (per-list advisory lock; `app.actor_uid`), 8.2, 8.5 (recipe-import events; the queue choice is left to the push task), new 8.6 (worker cron and `share_import_worker_key`), Q17 (dismissing a failed share is open: the plan has no dismiss RPC, so failed shares show Try again only). Correction to plan §0 item 5: `one_open_item_per_ingredient` does exist for the exact name; 7.3 now says the race fails the later same-name insert and leaves family twins both open, which the lock fixes. `docs/spikes.md` §2: outcome recorded (option C, generalized to scoped `device_credentials`, built first for share import). AGENTS.md: `share_import_worker_key` vault line. Jest before (197 suites, 5400 passed, 2 skipped), lint and tsc pass; no `supabase/` change. No real AI calls.

Server: share import jobs (plan §4): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261210093000_share_imports.sql`: `public.share_imports` as in spec 5 (`status` defaults to `received`; indexes for due work, leases, per user and retention; the `set_updated_at` trigger; RLS on, no client grants) and the view `my_share_imports` (runs as its owner, filters `user_id = auth.uid()`, leaves out `page`/`extraction`/hash/owner/lease; `select` to `authenticated` only). Service-role functions: `claim_share_import(p_kinds text[] default null)` (kinds `extracting`/`committing`, null for both; returns `setof share_imports`, the row with its page; an expired lease that has already used 8 attempts is failed with `lease_lost`/transient instead of claimed), `reserve_share_import` (answers `check_recipe_import_limit`'s `ok`/`user_limit`/`daily_limit`/`monthly_limit`; the worker maps them to its codes), `save_share_extraction`, `release_share_import` (returns the new status; transient backoff from `private.share_import_backoff(attempts)`, 30 s/2 min/10 min/1 h/6 h plus up to 20 % jitter, unless `p_next_attempt_at` is given; waiting is `rate_limited` only, due the next minute, attempts − 1; permanent keeps `p_resets_at`; `failed` nulls `page`). All of them check the lease through `private.leased_share_import` and raise `lease_lost` (55000): save and reserve need an unexpired lease, release only a matching token. For `authenticated`: `retry_share_import` (failed → received, attempts 0, error cleared, `metered_at` kept; any other status is returned unchanged; P0002 for another user's id) and `share_import_status`. The daily cron `share-imports-retention` (03:53) runs `private.share_imports_retention()`; the extraction purge counts from `coalesce(committed_at, updated_at)`. Left to later tasks: the worker cron and the failure push. Spec 6.12 gained one line on `p_kinds`, the lost-lease rule and `lease_lost`'s code. **Tests:** pgTAP `68_share_imports.test.sql` (75): two real claimers through `dblink` (installed inside the test transaction; it connects over `inet_server_addr()` because loopback is trust and dblink needs a password; it commits its own rows and deletes them); access (table, the view's columns and rows, anon, function grants, status); every transition; expired and foreign leases refused; reserving twice charges once; `daily_limit` charges nothing and keeps `resets_at`; the 8th attempt fails the job; Try again keeps the id and doesn't charge again; retention; cascade on user deletion. **Checks:** db reset + `supabase test db` (all pass), jest (207 suites, 5492 passed, 2 skipped), lint, tsc. No existing test changed. No real AI calls. **Cleanup needed:** a scratch probe `supabase/tests/zz_probe_wt10.test.sql` (it only prints extensions and cron jobs) is still in the worktree, untracked, because deleting it needed approval I couldn't get. Delete it; don't commit it.

Real-device check of share import on the server (plan §9, last row): no code to write. Added the full check to manual-checks.md and checked off the task. The setup: two iPhones on development builds pointed at local Supabase over the LAN, functions served, the four Vault secrets seeded, the cron runs checked in Studio, and A's device credential registered. Then seven cases, each saying what to look for in `share_imports`, on each phone and in the pushes. No tests added (no code changed). **Checks:** jest 212 / 5652 passed, 2 skipped, before and after; lint and tsc clean. No real AI calls. NEEDS A MANUAL CHECK: on two iPhones (A the sharer, B in the same household) with development builds pointed at the Mac's LAN IP, local Supabase running, functions served and the Vault secrets seeded: (1) force-quit the app on A, share a recipe from Safari and dismiss the sheet at once: the `share_imports` row reaches `done` without the app being opened; (2) the same in airplane mode: no row until A reconnects, then `done`, imported once; (3) lock the phone right after Save: `done`, and the ready push shows on the lock screen; (4) force-quit before sharing, open the app right after and force-quit it again: one row, one recipe, the items added once, no stuck card; (5) B gets the recipe and its list items through sync, plus the household push, while A's app is never opened; (6) A gets "Lemon pasta is ready" (tapping it opens the recipe), and for a page that isn't a recipe "Couldn't import that recipe" / "That page doesn't look like a recipe" (tapping it opens the failed import on the Recipes tab); (7) with Settings > Notifications > Recipe imports off, neither push is sent, but the imports still finish. Full steps in manual-checks.md.
manualChecks: Real-device check of share import on the server (plan §9, last row). **Setup:** two iPhones, A (the sharer) and B (another member of the same household), each with a development build (`eas build --profile development`, so the App Group, the shared Keychain group and push are provisioned; push also needs `docs/push-setup.md` §1–2) and `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://<Mac's Wi-Fi IP>:55321` (README, "Run on a device"), both on the Mac's Wi-Fi. On the Mac: `supabase start`, `supabase functions serve --env-file supabase/functions/.env`, and seed the four Vault secrets in AGENTS.md (`project_url`, `notifications_worker_key`, `photo_cleanup_key`, `share_import_worker_key`); in Studio (http://127.0.0.1:55323) `cron.job_run_details` shows the `share-import-worker` and `send-notifications` jobs succeeding each minute. Sign in on both phones and allow notifications; open the app once on A so it registers its device credential (one live `device_credentials` row for A's user); leave Settings > Notifications > Recipe imports on. Use a different real recipe page in Safari each time, with "Add to list" on and a list chosen. After each case wait up to two minutes (a worker tick to extract, one to commit): A's new `share_imports` row ends `done` with `recipe_id` (and `applied_list_id`, `items_added` when it added to a list), and the recipe and its items show once, not twice, when A next opens the app. **1. Dismiss at once, app force-quit:** force-quit the app on A; in Safari, Share > The Perfect Bite > Save, and swipe the sheet away / go home the moment "Saved. We'll prepare it in the background." shows. Don't open the app: the row appears within seconds and reaches `done`. **2. Airplane mode, then reconnect:** force-quit the app, turn on airplane mode, share and dismiss as in 1. The sheet says the same; no row appears. Turn airplane mode off (Wi-Fi back on) without opening the app: the background upload goes through and the row reaches `done`. If it hasn't after five minutes, open the app: the reconcile submits it, and it's still imported only once. **3. Locked right after sharing:** share, Save, and press the side button at once. Leave the phone locked: the row reaches `done` and the "ready" push shows on the lock screen. **4. Force-quit before sharing and right after:** force-quit the app, share and save, then open the app and force-quit it again within a second or two. One `share_imports` row for that envelope id, one recipe, the items added once; on the next open there's no stuck pending card on the Recipes tab. **5. Second household phone:** with B's app open on the chosen list, and again with it backgrounded, share from A without opening A's app. B gets the recipe in Recipes and its ingredients on the list through sync, A never having opened the app; B gets the household push ("<A> added <recipe> (<n> items) to <list>", with list pushes on) and no "ready" push. **6. The sharer's pushes:** A gets "*Lemon pasta* is ready" (the recipe's name; body "Added to <list>", or "Saved to <household>" when not adding to a list), on A's devices only; tapping it opens the recipe. Share a page that isn't a recipe (a news article): the row ends `failed` with `error_code` `not_a_recipe`, and A gets "Couldn't import that recipe" / "That page doesn't look like a recipe"; tapping it opens the Recipes tab with the failed import and Try again. **7. Recipe imports off:** on A, Settings > Notifications > Recipe imports off (`notification_settings.recipe_imports` false for A's user). Share a recipe and a non-recipe page: the rows still end `done` / `failed`, and A gets neither push (B's household push for the recipe still comes). Turn it back on afterwards.

title: `share-ingest` Edge Function
text: `share-ingest` Edge Function (plan §7 share-ingest, §8). POST with `Authorization: Bearer` and either a device credential (scope `share.ingest`, through `verifyDeviceCredential`) or a user session, and an `Idempotency-Key` equal to the envelope id. The user always comes from authentication; an envelope `userId` that differs is refused with 403 `account_mismatch`. Validates with `ShareEnvelopeSchema` (now with optional `userId` and `v`), an http(s) URL, a household the user belongs to and a list in it; aggregate body over 2.5 MB is 413. `insert … on conflict (id) do nothing` with `payload_hash` (sha256 of the canonical url, household, list, `addToList` and page): new or identical returns 202 `{ id, status }`, the same id with another owner or payload 409 `operation_conflict`. A per-credential limit (30 a minute, a row in the safety-limits table) answers 429. A kill switch (an AI or feature setting, as the other functions use) answers 503. After accepting it starts the worker with `EdgeRuntime.waitUntil` (best effort only). Deno tests for each answer, a resubmit after a lost response, and the mismatch and conflict cases.
notes: `share-ingest` Edge Function (plan §7, §8): DONE, checked off. **Function** `supabase/functions/share-ingest/` (`index.ts`, `request.ts`, `handler.ts`). `verify_jwt = false` is set in `config.toml` because a device credential isn't a JWT. `withSupabase({ auth: 'none' })` supplies the service-role client. A bearer token with dots is checked as a session through `createSupabaseContext(req, { auth: 'user' })`; any other token goes through `verifyDeviceCredential(…, 'share.ingest')`. Answers, in the order they're checked: 405 · 503 `unavailable` with Retry-After 3600 when `SHARE_IMPORT=off` (before auth) · 401 `unauthorized` · 413 over 2.5 MB (declared or streamed) · 400 `invalid_request` / `invalid_url` (`ShareEnvelopeSchema`) · 400 when `Idempotency-Key` isn't the envelope id (case-insensitive) · 403 `account_mismatch` · 429 `rate_limited` (credentials only). Then the RPC answers: 409 `operation_conflict`, 403 `not_a_member`, 400 `invalid_request` (list not in the household), or 202 `{ id, status }` (`no-store`). `payload_hash` is the sha256 of canonical JSON (keys sorted) of `{ url: canonicalRecipeUrl, householdId, listId (lower-cased), addToList (missing = true), page }`. After a 202 for a job that isn't `done` or `failed`, it POSTs `share-import-worker` with the secret key as `apikey` under `EdgeRuntime.waitUntil`. Errors there are only logged, and that worker is the next task. Each accepted share logs one line (status, via, bytes, JSON-LD count, text bytes), never the page or the token. **Schema:** `ShareEnvelopeSchema` gains optional `v: 2` and `userId` (uuid). **Migration** `20261211120000_share_ingest.sql`: `authenticate_device_credential(hash, scope)` returns `(user_id, credential_id)`, because the per-credential limit and `share_imports.credential_id` need the id. `use_device_credential` is now a wrapper over it, with the same signature and answers. **`verifyDeviceCredential` now returns `{ userId, credentialId }`.** Nothing called it yet; its Deno tests changed to match, and the spec line is updated. The `share_ingest` safety limit (30 a minute, no daily limit) is added to `ai_safety_limits` (the check constraint and `private.safety_limit_keys()`). `check_share_ingest_limit(credential_id)` counts it per credential in `private.share_ingest_usage`. `ingest_share_import(…)` (service role) answers `(outcome, status)`. It checks, in order: an existing id (same user and hash → accepted with its current status, so a resubmit works even after leaving the household; otherwise conflict); the household (as given, else the list's, else the default list's, else the user's first by `joined_at`); membership; and the list belonging to that household (archived or deleted lists are accepted, and the worker falls back). Then it runs `insert … on conflict (id) do nothing`, re-reading the row if it loses a race. **Choices:** an envelope with no household and no list (from an older extension) is resolved as above instead of refused; spec 6.12 now says so. A list that doesn't exist on the server yet (created offline and not pushed) gets a 400. **Admin:** `share_ingest` is added to `admin/lib/safety-limits.ts` ("Share uploads", hint "Per device credential, not AI"), because the drift test requires it. **Tests:**

title: Worker: extraction
text: Worker: extraction (plan §4 Workers and Errors). Refactor `supabase/functions/import-recipe/handler.ts` so the extraction (page from the request or `fetchPage`, `extract`, the URL cache for server-fetched pages only, categorize, the response) is `extractForImport(request, deps)`, called by `importRecipe` after its plan check and limit as now (`import-recipe` behaves exactly as before; its tests pass). New Edge Function `share-import-worker` (service role, a Vault-secret key like `send-notifications`): it loops `claim_share_import` until nothing is due or about 50 s have passed; for `extracting` it runs `requireFeature`, then `reserve_share_import`, then `extractForImport` with the job's page (never cached by URL), with no database transaction open during the fetch or the model call, then `save_share_extraction`; errors map to transient, waiting (`rate_limited`) or permanent (`not_a_recipe`, `invalid_url`, `not_entitled`, `daily_limit`, `limit_reached`, with `resets_at` kept) through `release_share_import`. A pg_cron job calls the worker every minute through pg_net with Vault secrets `project_url` and `share_import_worker_key` (document the secret in AGENTS.md if task 1 didn't). Deno tests with fake stores: a crash after `reserve` doesn't charge again on retry, a lost lease stops the save, and each error class.

It loops `claim_share_import(['extracting'])` until nothing is due or 50 s have passed (it claims only `extracting` until the commit task adds `committing`). For each job it runs `requireFeature`, then `importUrlKey` (so `invalid_url` and the kill switch fail before charging), `reserve_share_import`, `extractForImport` with the job's page (when the page is null or malformed, the URL is fetched and cached as in-app), and `save_share_extraction`. On `lease_lost` (55000) from save or release it stops without writing. title: Worker: atomic commit
text: Worker: atomic commit (plan §5, §6). In the worker, for `committing`: resolve the destination as `resolveImportTarget` does (the list if live, unarchived and in the household, else the user's `default_list_id`; recipe-only into the household; with no lists, recipe-only with `applied_list_id` null and a `list_gone` flag in the receipt), read the snapshot (plan §5 Planning step 2) with the service role, plan with `planRecipeImport` and ids `uuidv5(op id + ':' + purpose + ':' + index)`, and call `commit_share_import(p_id, p_lease, p_target, p_writes, p_preconditions)`. The RPC (security definer, service role only), in one transaction: lock the job row (an existing `committed_at` returns the stored receipt; a wrong or expired lease raises `lease_lost`); recheck membership and destination (`destination_changed`); take the per-list advisory lock; check every precondition with rows `for update` (`plan_conflict`); set `app.actor_uid`; apply every write through `private.apply_mutation(write, user_id)` with no subtransaction, so any rejection rolls everything back, with HLCs assigned in the RPC (device `srv`, wall time the larger of `clock_timestamp()` in ms and the largest `field_clock` wall among the touched rows plus 1, counter the write index); write the receipt (`recipe_id`, `applied_list_id`, `items_added`, `items_combined`, `committed_at`), `status = 'done'`, clear the lease and `page`; return the receipt. On `plan_conflict` or `destination_changed` the worker rereads and replans up to 3 times, then releases as transient; a member who left, or no household, is permanent. pgTAP: a retry after commit returns the receipt and adds nothing; an item checked between plan and commit raises `plan_conflict` and the replan reopens it; an item reopened and added to meanwhile keeps the new contribution; a concurrent device amount edit and the import both survive (the import's contribution on top); two imports into one list with shared ingredients; a removed member writes nothing; activity is logged as the sharer; the household push event is queued. A Deno integration test against local Supabase runs one share end to end, from ingest to receipt.
notes: **Worker: atomic commit (share import on the server).** Migration `20261215101700_commit_share_import.sql`: `commit_share_import(p_id, p_lease, p_target, p_writes, p_preconditions)` (security definer, service_role only) locks the job (a set `committed_at` returns the stored receipt, whatever the lease; otherwise `private.leased_share_import` → `lease_lost` 55000), validates `p_target` (`household_id`, `list_id`, `list_gone`, `recipe_id`, `items_added`, `items_combined`), rechecks membership and the list (`destination_changed` 40001), takes the per-list advisory lock, checks each precondition in `private.share_import_precondition` with rows `for update` (`plan_conflict` 40001: `combine` live/unchecked on the list; `reopen` live, `checked_at` equal to the planned ms, same live contribution set; `new` no live item with the key, by own name or, when the household combines languages, by family; `recipeAbsent` no row at all with the id, since a deleted one would only be patched; `recipeReuse` live in the household), only accepts the planner's six tables, computes the wall (max of `clock_timestamp()` ms and the largest `field_clock` wall on the touched rows + 1), applies each write through `private.apply_mutation` with HLC `<wall>-<index hex>-srv` and no subtransaction, then the receipt (`done`, lease and `page` cleared). Activity: `app.actor_uid` is set and the per-row triggers are suppressed (`private.suppress_activity`) for the writes, and the one `recipe.imported_from_share` entry (area `recipes`, `{ household, recipe, recipe_id, list, items_added, items_combined }`) is inserted directly, because the trigger's `app.activity_action` path always writes area `household`; the "ready" push queue is left to the next task. Worker: new `share-import-worker/commit.ts` (`resolveTarget`: the list if live, unarchived and in the share's household, else the default list, else the share household's first list, else any; no lists → recipe-only with `list_gone`; not a member or household gone → permanent `not_a_member`. `readSnapshot` mirrors the device's `addSnapshot`. `planCommit` calls `planRecipeImport` with the recipe id `uuidv5(op id)` under `IMPORT_ID_NAMESPACE`, or `uuidv5(op id:recipe:0)` if a deleted recipe holds it, and `uuidv5(op id:purpose:index)` for the rest; `uuidV5` is a crypto.subtle implementation). `handler.ts` now claims both phases (`kinds` dep, default both) and runs `commitJob`: replans up to `MAX_REPLANS` = 3 times after a conflict (4 commits), then releases transient with the conflict's code; `CommitRefusedError` → permanent. `store.ts` has `createShareImportCommitStore` (PostgREST reads with the service role, 40001 conflicts mapped to `CommitConflictError`). `IMPORT_ID_NAMESPACE` moved to `src/shared/domain/recipe-import.ts` (re-exported from `src/features/recipes/import.ts`, unchanged for callers). Changed existing tests: `share-import-worker/handler.test.ts` setup passes `commitStore` (a stub) and `kinds: ['extracting']`, its fake rows carry `list_id`/`add_to_list`/`extraction`, and `RunResult` has `committed`. New tests: pgTAP `73_commit_share_import` (56: privileges; a full commit with its receipt, recipe, item, amount, usage count and `srv` HLC; the activity entry as the sharer; the household `items_added` event from the sharer; a retry after commit returns the receipt and adds nothing; wrong, expired and non-committing leases; bad target; recipe-only with `list_gone`; archived list and another household are `destination_changed`; a removed member writes nothing; a rejected write rolls back the earlier ones; a table outside the plan refused; recipe preconditions; an item checked between plan and commit conflicts and the replan reopens it with an HLC one past the device's skewed clock; an item reopened and added to meanwhile keeps the new amount; a device amount edit before and after the commit both survive with the import's on top; two imports with a shared ingredient end as one item with both amounts; `new` against a checked item). Deno `commit.test.ts` (20: uuidV5 against Python's documented vector, resolveTarget fallbacks, readSnapshot with and without combine-languages, planCommit ids, deleted-id fallback, reuse by canonical URL with Combine and reopen, and the phase: commit, replan after a check, 4 conflicts → transient, destination change, left member, list gone, lost lease, internal errors), 2 more in `store.test.ts`, and `integration.test.ts` (skipped unless `SHARE_IMPORT_INTEGRATION=1`; run with `--env-file` holding that and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`): ingest → extract (mock models) → commit → receipt against local Supabase, a retry returning the receipt, and a second share Combining into the same items. It passed. **Checks:** I didn't run jest before starting (the previous entry's 209 suites / 5602 passed is the baseline); after: 209 suites, 5602 passed, 2 skipped. `yarn expo lint` and `yarn tsc --noEmit` clean; Deno worker 49 passed (1 ignored), `_shared` 101, share-ingest 26; `supabase db reset` and `supabase test db` (72 files, 2432 tests) pass. The local database is shared with the other parallel agents and was reset under me once mid-run; the final reset and test run were back to back. No real AI calls.

title: "Recipe ready" and "Couldn't import" pushes
text: "Recipe ready" and "Couldn't import" pushes (plan §10, spec 4.13). Migration: `notification_settings.recipe_imports boolean not null default true`, and a queue entry when a share import reaches `done` (from `commit_share_import`) or `failed` (from `release_share_import`), on `household_events` or a sibling queue (say which). `send-notifications` sends to the sharer's own push tokens only, sent at once rather than grouped, respecting `recipe_imports` and quiet hours: "*Lemon pasta* is ready" (data `url` `/recipe/<id>`) or "Couldn't import that recipe" with the reason in the body (data `url` the Recipes tab, which shows the failed imports). Allow those urls in `src/features/push/receiving.ts`; a recipe not on the device yet gets a pull first, as lists do. Settings > Notifications gets a **Recipe imports** switch (detail "When a recipe you shared is ready, or couldn't be imported") after the existing switches, saved like them through `src/features/push/settings.ts`. title: App: device credential
text: App: device credential (plan §2, §3 account binding). With `expo-secure-store` (check its SDK docs for `accessGroup` and `AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY`), keep `{ token, userId, installationId, expiresAt }` in a dedicated shared Keychain access group; the installation id is created once per install and kept across sign-outs. Add `keychain-access-groups` to the app's `ios.entitlements` in `app.json`, to `targets/share-recipe/expo-target.config.js`, and to the share extension's entry in the EAS `appExtensions` entitlements in `app.json`; never edit `ios/`. After sign-in, and on foreground when under 30 days remain, call `register-device-credential` and store the answer. On sign-out, call `revoke_my_device_credential` when online and always delete the Keychain item. On account switch, the new user registers under the same installation id. The list snapshot (`siri/lists.json`) gains the signed-in `userId`. Jest for register, renew, sign-out online and offline, and account switch. Check the built entitlements of both targets after `yarn expo prebuild --clean` in a scratch copy (or say how), and add the check to `manual-checks.md`.

New `src/features/auth/device-credential.ts`: `{ token, userId, installationId, expiresAt }` as JSON in Keychain item `share.credential`, service `com.jgp.perfectbite.device-credential` (stored by expo-secure-store as `<service>:no-auth`, noted for the Swift reader), access group `4537GH756L.com.jgp.perfectbite.shared`, `AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY`. text: App: reconcile shares with the server (plan §7). Replace the share drain (`src/features/recipes/share-drain.ts`, started from `src/features/app-data.tsx`) on the same triggers: read `share/pending/*.json` and keep envelopes whose `userId` is the signed-in user (an envelope without `userId` counts as the current user's); `share_import_status(ids)`; for ids the server has, delete the envelope and its `share/upload/` and `share/upload-state/` files; submit the rest to `share-ingest` with the user's session and the envelope id, deleting the local files once the server accepts them; leave another user's envelopes alone. The Recipes tab's imports card shows the user's share imports from `my_share_imports` (queued, importing, failed with its reason, including "You've reached today's limit…" with the reset time), and Try again on a failed share calls `retry_share_import` with the same id. `failed_imports` stays for in-app imports. Realtime or a pull after a push refreshes the card. notes: **App: reconcile shares with the server (share import on the server, plan §7, spec 4.10 step 5).** DONE, checked off. text: Share extension: background upload and completion (plan §3). In `targets/share-recipe/ShareViewController.swift` and `targets/_shared/ShareQueue.swift`: the envelope gains `userId` (from the snapshot) and `v: 2` (update `ShareEnvelopeSchema`, the Swift `Codable` and the contract test together); after the atomic write, if the shared Keychain has a credential for the same `userId` that hasn't expired, write the request body to `share/upload/<id>.json` and start a `URLSessionUploadTask` from that file on a background `URLSession` with identifier `com.jgp.perfectbite.share.upload` and `sharedContainerIdentifier` `group.com.jgp.perfectbite`, `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `Idempotency-Key: <id>`, to the `share-ingest` URL from the extension's Info.plist (set through `targets/share-recipe/expo-target.config.js` from the app config); record `share/upload-state/<id>.json`. The sheet says "Saved. We'll prepare it in the background." (both switch states; update `ShareChoice.savedMessage` and its tests). Add a local Expo module (`modules/`, an `ExpoAppDelegateSubscriber`; check the SDK's Expo Modules docs) that, for that identifier in `application(_:handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession:completionHandler:)`, recreates the session, takes its delegate events (a 2xx deletes `share/upload/<id>.json` and marks the state accepted; anything else leaves both for reconciliation) and calls the completion handler. Nothing treats a response as final; the local envelope stays until reconciliation sees the server has it. Swift unit tests where the existing targets have them, otherwise a contract test of the files written; lint and typecheck pass.
notes: Share extension: background upload and completion (plan §3): `ShareQueue.Envelope` gains `v` (2) and `userId` (from the list snapshot; `ShareEnvelopeSchema` already had both as optional). `ShareQueue.enqueue` returns the bytes written, and `ShareModel.save` then calls `ShareUpload.start`. It reads the device credential from the shared Keychain the way expo-secure-store writes it (`ShareCredential`). Only when the credential is for the same `userId` (ignoring case) and hasn't expired, it writes `share/upload/<id>.json` (the envelope bytes, the same payload the app's reconcile submits) and `share/upload-state/<id>.json` (`{ startedAt, attempts: 1 }`), then starts a `URLSessionUploadTask` from that file. The task runs on the background session `com.jgp.perfectbite.share.upload` (`sharedContainerIdentifier` the App Group), with `Authorization: Bearer` and `Idempotency-Key`, and posts to `ShareIngestURL` from the extension's Info.plist. The Info.plist value is `$(SHARE_INGEST_URL)`. @bacons/apple-targets 5 has no option for Info.plist keys or build settings, so `targets/share-recipe/expo-target.config.js` registers an Xcode-project mod (`withXcodeProjectBeta`). Registered before apple-targets adds the target, it runs after it, and sets that build setting on the ShareRecipe target to `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` + `/functions/v1/share-ingest` (the env loaded with the app config). With no URL it removes the setting, and the extension skips the upload. Added `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` to the extension's ATS so it can reach local Supabase over LAN http. The sheet says "Saved. We'll prepare it in the background." in both switch states: `ShareChoice.savedMessage` is now a constant, and `shareSavedMessage(addToList)` became `SHARE_SAVED_MESSAGE` in save-choice.ts (its test changed because the behavior did). New local Expo module `modules/share-upload` (apple only, `appDelegateSubscribers: ["ShareUploadAppDelegate"]`). For our session identifier it recreates the background session once. On a 2xx its delegate deletes `share/upload/<id>.json` and sets `accepted`/`acceptedAt` in the state file (only if that file still exists); anything else leaves both. It calls the completion handler from `urlSessionDidFinishEvents`; for other identifiers it calls the handler at once. Only reconciliation deletes the envelope. **Tests:** `share.test.ts`: new `share-envelope.v2.json` fixture as Swift writes it, v2 without userId, a bad `v`/`userId` rejected, older fixtures have neither. `share-extension.test.ts`, new contract tests: on both Swift sides the session id, App Group and paths match `app-group.ts`; the Keychain names match `device-credential.ts`; the upload starts after the atomic write, with the headers and from the body file; the state fields; the 2xx rule on both sides and no envelope deletion; the module config and subscriber shape; the Info.plist key; `shareIngestUrl` cases; `setShareIngestUrl` touches only ShareRecipe; the registered mod sets the URL from the env. `save-choice.test.ts` updated. We'll prepare it in the background."; the server imports; the app reconciles instead of draining; failures and Try again from server state on the sharer's devices only; `daily_limit`/`limit_reached` fail with their reason; dead/archived list → default list, no lists → recipe-only with "Saved *Lemon pasta*. Its list was gone, so nothing was added."; a sharer who left fails permanently, per plan §10, replacing the old "household of the default list" fallback for shares; in-app imports stay on the device; imports card rewritten over envelopes + `my_share_imports`; no share toast), 4.12 (`share-import-worker` checks `recipe_import`; `share_ingest` safety row, 30/min per credential; activity actor `coalesce(auth.uid(), app.actor_uid)` and a `recipe.imported_from_share` catalog row; **Device credentials** bullet with audited `admin_revoke_device_credentials` and the user-page button), 4.13 (the two sharer pushes, `/recipe/<id>` and `/recipes` urls, **Recipe imports** switch; household "added" push now at server commit), 5 (`device_credentials`, `share_imports` (plus `title` and a `list_gone` receipt column, not in the plan), `my_share_imports`, `notification_settings.recipe_imports`, RLS and RPC access, retention job), new 6.12 (the three functions, jobs and states, errors, metering, the commit, privacy, rollout), 7.2 (the server as a writer through `private.apply_mutation`, `srv` HLCs, no pull change), 7.3 (per-list advisory lock; `app.actor_uid`), 8.2, 8.5 (recipe-import events; the queue choice is left to the push task), new 8.6 (worker cron and `share_import_worker_key`), Q17 (dismissing a failed share is open: the plan has no dismiss RPC, so failed shares show Try again only). Correction to plan §0 item 5: `one_open_item_per_ingredient` does exist for the exact name; 7.3 now says the race fails the later same-name insert and leaves family twins both open, which the lock fixes. `docs/spikes.md` §2: outcome recorded (option C, generalized to scoped `device_credentials`, built first for share import). Server: share import jobs (plan §4): DONE, checked off. Migration `20261210093000_share_imports.sql`: `public.share_imports` as in spec 5 (`status` defaults to `received`; indexes for due work, leases, per user and retention; the `set_updated_at` trigger; RLS on, no client grants) and the view `my_share_imports` (runs as its owner, filters `user_id = auth.uid()`, leaves out `page`/`extraction`/hash/owner/lease; `select` to `authenticated` only). Service-role functions: `claim_share_import(p_kinds text[] default null)` (kinds `extracting`/`committing`, null for both; returns `setof share_imports`, the row with its page; an expired lease that has already used 8 attempts is failed with `lease_lost`/transient instead of claimed), `reserve_share_import` (answers `check_recipe_import_limit`'s `ok`/`user_limit`/`daily_limit`/`monthly_limit`; the worker maps them to its codes), `save_share_extraction`, `release_share_import` (returns the new status; transient backoff from `private.share_import_backoff(attempts)`, 30 s/2 min/10 min/1 h/6 h plus up to 20 % jitter, unless `p_next_attempt_at` is given; waiting is `rate_limited` only, due the next minute, attempts − 1; permanent keeps `p_resets_at`; `failed` nulls `page`). manualChecks: Real-device check of share import on the server (plan §9, last row). **Setup:** two iPhones, A (the sharer) and B (another member of the same household), each with a development build (`eas build --profile development`, so the App Group, the shared Keychain group and push are provisioned; push also needs `docs/push-setup.md` §1–2) and `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://<Mac's Wi-Fi IP>:55321` (README, "Run on a device"), both on the Mac's Wi-Fi. On the Mac: `supabase start`, `supabase functions serve --env-file supabase/functions/.env`, and seed the four Vault secrets in AGENTS.md (`project_url`, `notifications_worker_key`, `photo_cleanup_key`, `share_import_worker_key`); in Studio (http://127.0.0.1:55323) `cron.job_run_details` shows the `share-import-worker` and `send-notifications` jobs succeeding each minute. Sign in on both phones and allow notifications; open the app once on A so it registers its device credential (one live `device_credentials` row for A's user); leave Settings > Notifications > Recipe imports on. Use a different real recipe page in Safari each time, with "Add to list" on and a list chosen. After each case wait up to two minutes (a worker tick to extract, one to commit): A's new `share_imports` row ends `done` with `recipe_id` (and `applied_list_id`, `items_added` when it added to a list), and the recipe and its items show once, not twice, when A next opens the app. **1. Dismiss at once, app force-quit:** force-quit the app on A; in Safari, Share > The Perfect Bite > Save, and swipe the sheet away / go home the moment "Saved. We'll prepare it in the background." shows. Don't open the app: the row appears within seconds and reaches `done`. **2. Airplane mode, then reconnect:** force-quit the app, turn on airplane mode, share and dismiss as in 1. The sheet says the same; no row appears. Turn airplane mode off (Wi-Fi back on) without opening the app: the background upload goes through and the row reaches `done`. If it hasn't after five minutes, open the app: the reconcile submits it, and it's still imported only once. **3. Locked right after sharing:** share, Save, and press the side button at once. Leave the phone locked: the row reaches `done` and the "ready" push shows on the lock screen. **4. Force-quit before sharing and right after:** force-quit the app, share and save, then open the app and force-quit it again within a second or two. One `share_imports` row for that envelope id, one recipe, the items added once; on the next open there's no stuck pending card on the Recipes tab. **5. Second household phone:** with B's app open on the chosen list, and again with it backgrounded, share from A without opening A's app. B gets the recipe in Recipes and its ingredients on the list through sync, A never having opened the app; B gets the household push ("<A> added <recipe> (<n> items) to <list>", with list pushes on) and no "ready" push. **6. The sharer's pushes:** A gets "*Lemon pasta* is ready" (the recipe's name; body "Added to <list>", or "Saved to <household>" when not adding to a list), on A's devices only; tapping it opens the recipe. Share a page that isn't a recipe (a news article): the row ends `failed` with `error_code` `not_a_recipe`, and A gets "Couldn't import that recipe" / "That page doesn't look like a recipe"; tapping it opens the Recipes tab with the failed import and Try again. **7. Recipe imports off:** on A, Settings > Notifications > Recipe imports off (`notification_settings.recipe_imports` false for A's user). Share a recipe and a non-recipe page: the rows still end `done` / `failed`, and A gets neither push (B's household push for the recipe still comes). Turn it back on afterwards.

Add `updateFailedPhotoImport(id, { pages, householdId, listId })` for the review sheet (deletes removed pages' files). Dismiss, `wipeLocalData` and a launch prune (rows older than 30 days, or whose files are missing) delete the folder too. `failedImportName` and the reason helpers cover rows without a url. title: Recipe collections, data
text: Recipe collections, data (no spec section yet: this task's text is the spec; mockups `docs/design/recipe-collections/`). A collection is a named set of recipes owned by a household, shared by every member, and a recipe can be in any number of them. Collections sit beside tags and Saved and don't replace them: tags stay the fixed vocabulary the AI fills, and Favorites (per person) and Want to try (a status) stay as they are. Supabase migration: `recipe_collections` (`id`, `household_id`, `name` text 1–40 chars trimmed, `created_by` set by the server, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`, `field_clock`) and `recipe_collection_recipes` (`collection_id`, `recipe_id`, `household_id`, `added_at`, `deleted_at`, `field_clock`, primary key `(collection_id, recipe_id)`, the recipe and collection in the same household). Both are household data through `apply_mutations` with field-level LWW (`name` and `deleted_at` on collections; `deleted_at` on memberships, keyed `{ collection_id, recipe_id }` like `recipe_favorites`), readable and writable by every member, with RLS and pgTAP tests (a non-member can't read or write; a membership can't point across households). Names are unique per household among live collections, compared ignoring case and accents; the app checks before writing, and if two devices race, both survive (no server constraint). Deleting a collection soft-deletes it and leaves its memberships (they're ignored while it's deleted); deleting a recipe leaves its memberships, so restoring it brings them back. Local Drizzle migration for both tables, push and pull in `src/sync/` like favorites, and `wipeLocalData` covers them. `src/features/recipes/collections.ts`: `createCollection(householdId, name)`, `renameCollection`, `deleteCollection`, `setRecipeInCollection(recipeId, collectionId, on)`, `addRecipesToCollection(collectionId, recipeIds)` (one transaction, skips ones already in), and live queries for a household's collections (A–Z, each with its live-recipe count and its first four recipes' photos for the cover) and a recipe's collections. Free on every plan, no limit. Unit tests for create (including a duplicate name refused), rename, delete, add and remove, batch add, the counts ignoring deleted recipes, and sync round-trips.
notes: Recipe collections, data: Supabase migration `20261218100000_recipe_collections.sql` (`recipe_collections` with a 1–40 trimmed-name check and server-set `created_by`; `recipe_collection_recipes` keyed `(collection_id, recipe_id)`, `added_at` insert-only; select-only RLS for members, Realtime publication; `apply_mutation` takes both, LWW on name/deleted_at and membership deleted_at, and refuses a membership whose collection or recipe isn't in its household). No server name-uniqueness constraint (the app checks). Local Drizzle migration `0032_recipe_collections`; both tables registered in mutate/push/pull/realtime, `purgeHousehold`, `wipeLocalData` and `src/test/db.ts`. `src/features/recipes/collections.ts`: `createCollection`/`renameCollection` (throw `CollectionNameError` with `empty`/`tooLong`/`duplicate`; `collectionNameProblem` lets the UI check first, ignoring case and accents), `deleteCollection`, `setRecipeInCollection`, `addRecipesToCollection` (one transaction, skips ones already in, returns how many it added, refuses other households' recipes), `useHouseholdCollections`/`readHouseholdCollections` (A–Z, live-recipe count, cover = first four recipes A–Z with `photoPath`/`imageUrl`) and `useRecipeCollections`/`readRecipeCollections`. **Tests added:** `collections.test.ts` (21: create, duplicate refused, other household's and deleted names free, length limits, rename, delete keeps memberships, add/remove/re-add outbox, no-op writes, cross-household refusals, batch add, counts ignoring deleted and removed recipes, cover, a recipe's collections, purge); a push test for both tables; pull tests (order, cursors, LWW both ways); pgTAP `76_recipe_collections.test.sql` (35). **Existing tests changed because the behavior changed:** the pull order lists in `pull.test.ts` (full and scoped pulls) now include the two tables; `09_realtime.test.sql` lists them as published; the local-wipe seed adds a collection and membership so the every-table test covers them. **Checks:** jest 214 suites, 5764 passed, 2 skipped; lint and tsc clean; `supabase db reset` and `supabase test db` pass. No real AI calls.

title: Recipe collections, filtering
text: Recipe collections, filtering (`docs/design/recipe-collections/` board E). The Filters sheet (Recipes tab and the plan slot sheet's panel, 4.16) gets a **Collections** group right after Saved: one pill per collection that has a live recipe in the user's households (a picked one stays so it can be turned off), A–Z; with several households, two with the same name show once and match both. OR within the group, AND with the other facets and the search, like the tag facets, and it counts toward the Filters button's number and **Show N recipes**. Add it to `recipe-filters.ts` and `recipe-filter-store.ts`; a deleted collection drops out of the picks. en and es strings. Unit tests for matching (OR within, AND across, same name in two households) and component tests for the group showing and hiding.
notes: Recipe collections, filtering (board E). Baseline jest before changes: 217 suites, 5848 passed, 2 skipped. `RecipeFilters` gains `collections` (picked collection names) and `FilterFacetKey` gains `'collections'`. Names compare by `collectionNameKey` (new in `recipe-filters.ts`, ignoring case and accents; `collections.ts` now uses it for its duplicate check), so one pick matches every collection with that name in any household. Matching is OR within the group and AND with the other facets and the search. Picks count in `activeFilterCount` (the Filters button and Show N recipes), and their chips come after Saved's and before Meal's, in pick order. `availableFilterFacets` takes a 4th `collections` argument (`CollectionsByRecipe`, recipe id → collection names) and adds the **Collections** group right after Saved: one pill per name that a collection holding one of the given recipes has, A–Z, with the same name shown once (the first spelling under a full-sensitivity collator), plus any picked name so it can be turned off. With no `collections` given there's no group, so the collection screen's sheet leaves it out. `matchesRecipeFilters`/`filterRecipes` take the same 4th argument. `collections.ts` adds `collectionsByRecipe`, `readCollectionsByRecipe`/`useCollectionsByRecipe` (live memberships in live collections, every household) and `readCollectionNames`. `recipe-filters.ts` adds `withoutGoneCollections`, and `recipe-filter-store.ts` adds `dropGoneCollectionFilters`, which the Recipes tab runs whenever the collections change. It reads the names straight from the database, because the live query starts empty and would otherwise wipe the picks on mount. A deleted collection drops out of the picks, and so does a renamed one, since picks are names. `RecipeFilterPanel` takes an optional `collections` prop. The Recipes tab, its filter sheet and the plan slot sheet pass it (the slot sheet reads once, like its favorites, so it shows only the household's collections). `slotSheetRecipes` takes `collections` in its options. The list's Add to recipe sheet doesn't get the group, because the task didn't name it. Untagged is unchanged: being in a collection doesn't make a recipe tagged. en/es string `recipes.filters.collections` ("Collections" / "Colecciones"). **Tests added:** `recipe-filters.test.ts` (14: name key, OR within, AND across, same name in two households with either spelling, no data or no membership, group order after Saved and first without Saved values, none without data, only collections with a recipe, a picked name staying, toggling by another spelling and leaving Untagged, the count, chips and their removal, `withoutGoneCollections`, the Spanish group name); `collections-browse.test.tsx` (6: the tab's sheet shows the group after Saved A–Z without the empty collection; picks narrow the count and the tab, with the Filters count and chips; the group hidden with no collection holding a recipe, while a picked one stays; two households with the same name shown once and matching both; a deleted collection dropping out of the picks; the collection's own sheet without the group); `collections.test.ts` (2: `readCollectionsByRecipe`/`readCollectionNames` leaving out deleted collections and memberships, `collectionsByRecipe`); `slot.test.tsx` (2: the slot panel's Collections group with only the household's collections that have recipes, a pick narrowing with chips, and no group without collections). No existing tests changed. **Checks:** jest 217 suites, 5872 passed, 2 skipped; lint and tsc clean. No supabase/ changes. No real AI calls.
